sentences.zh: 王舒

translations.literal: Wang Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu

sentences.zh: 王舒，字處明，丞相導之從弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Shu, courtesy name Chuming, was a younger male cousin of Chancellor Wang Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu, whose courtesy name was Chuming, was a cousin of Grand Chancellor Wang Dao.

sentences.zh: 父會，侍御史。

translations.literal: His father was Wang Hui, Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Wang Hui, had served as Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 舒少為從兄敦所知，以天下多故，不營當時名，恆處私門，潛心學植。

translations.literal: In his youth Shu was recognized by his older cousin Dun; because the realm was beset by troubles, he did not pursue contemporary renown, always remained within his private household, and devoted himself to study and self-cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: From an early age he had won the regard of his older cousin Wang Dun; with the empire in turmoil, he avoided chasing fashionable reputation, kept to his own doors, and immersed himself in scholarship.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，州禮命，太傅辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: When he was over forty, the province summoned him with ceremony, and the grand tutor summoned him; he accepted none of these.
translations.idiomatic: After he passed forty, both the provincial authorities and the grand tutor offered him appointments; he declined every one.

sentences.zh: 及敦為青州，舒往依焉。

translations.literal: When Dun became governor of Qingzhou, Shu went and attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun took up the governorship of Qingzhou, Wang Shu went to join him.

sentences.zh: 時敦被徵為秘書監，以寇難路險，輕騎歸洛陽，委棄公主。

translations.literal: At that time Dun was summoned to be Director of the Palace Library; because banditry made the roads perilous, he returned to Luoyang with a light escort of cavalry and abandoned the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Dun had just been recalled to serve as director of the Palace Library; citing rebel activity and dangerous roads, he rode back to Luoyang with only a small mounted escort, leaving his princess consort behind.

sentences.zh: 時輜重金寶甚多，親賓無不競取，惟舒一無所眄，益為敦所賞。

translations.literal: At that time the baggage contained very much gold and treasure; relatives and guests without exception competed to take them—only Shu looked at none of it, and all the more was he prized by Dun.
translations.idiomatic: The train was laden with gold and jewels; kinsmen and guests fell over one another grabbing what they could, but Wang Shu never so much as glanced at the loot, which only deepened Dun’s esteem for him.

sentences.zh: 及元帝鎮建康，因與諸父兄弟俱渡江委質焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan garrisoned Jiankang, he therefore crossed the river together with his various uncles and brothers and pledged allegiance there.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Jin established his headquarters at Jiankang, Wang Shu crossed the Yangzi with his uncles and brothers to offer his service at court.

sentences.zh: 參鎮東軍事，出補溧陽令。

translations.literal: He served as adviser on the staff of the general who garrisoned the east, then went out and was appointed magistrate of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the staff of the commander who held the east, then was posted out as magistrate of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 明帝之為東中郎將，妙選上佐，以舒為司馬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was Eastern General of the Gentlemen of the Household, he discriminatingly selected senior aides and appointed Shu as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir-apparent as Eastern General of the Gentlemen of the Household, Emperor Ming handpicked his senior staff and named Wang Shu marshal of his command.

sentences.zh: 轉後將軍、宣城公褚裒諮議參軍，遷軍司，固辭不受。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be adviser on the staff of General of the Rear and Duke of Xuancheng Chu Pou, was promoted to army director, firmly declined, and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to serve as adviser under General of the Rear and Duke of Xuancheng Chu Pou, then was promoted to director of the army staff; he repeatedly refused the latter post and never took it up.

sentences.zh: 裒鎮廣陵，復以舒為車騎司馬。

translations.literal: When Pou garrisoned Guangling, he again appointed Shu as chariot-and-horse marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu Pou took command at Guangling, he again named Wang Shu chariot-and-horse marshal.

sentences.zh: 頻領望府，咸稱明練。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he headed prestigious administrations; all called him clear and experienced.
translations.idiomatic: He served in one eminent office after another, and everywhere he went colleagues praised his clarity and seasoned judgment.

sentences.zh: 裒薨，遂代裒鎮，除北中郎將、監青徐二州軍事。

translations.literal: When Pou died, he then replaced Pou in command, was appointed General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the North, and supervised military affairs of the two provinces Qing and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: After Chu Pou died, Wang Shu succeeded him in the command, receiving appointment as General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the North with supervisory authority over military affairs in Qingzhou and Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，征國子博士，加散騎常侍，未拜，轉少府。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Erudit of the National Academy, was given the additional title Cavalry-in-Attendance Without Specification, had not yet assumed office, and was transferred to Minister of the Lesser Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled to court as erudit of the National Academy and granted the concurrent title of cavalry attendant-at-large; before he could take up those duties he was reassigned as minister of the Lesser Treasury.

sentences.zh: 太甯初，徙廷尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taining reign, he was moved to be Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taining era he was transferred to the post of minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 敦表舒為鷹揚將軍、荊州刺史、領護南蠻校尉、監荊州沔南諸軍事。

translations.literal: Dun memorialized that Shu be General Who Displays Ferocity, Inspector of Jingzhou, concurrently Colonel of the Southern Man, and supervise all military affairs south of the Han in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun petitioned the throne to appoint Wang Shu General Who Displays Ferocity, inspector of Jingzhou, with the additional titles of colonel of the Southern Man and supervisor of all forces south of the Han River in that province.

sentences.zh: 及敦敗，王含父子俱奔舒，舒遣軍逆之，並沈于江。

translations.literal: When Dun was defeated, Wang Han father and son both fled to Shu; Shu dispatched troops to meet them and together drowned them in the river.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun’s defeat, Wang Han and his son fled to Wang Shu, who sent troops to intercept them and had both men drowned in the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 進都督荊州、平西將軍、假節。

translations.literal: He was advanced to governor-general of Jingzhou, General Who Pacifies the West, and was given the ceremonial tally.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to area commander-in-chief for Jingzhou, enfeoffed as General Who Pacifies the West, and invested with the credential axe.

sentences.zh: 尋以陶侃代舒，遷舒為安南將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long Tao Kan replaced Shu; Shu was transferred to be General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Tao Kan was sent to replace him, and Wang Shu was moved to the posts of General Who Guards the South and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 舒疾病，不樂越嶺，朝議亦以其有功，不應遠出，乃徙為湘州刺史，將軍、都督、持節如故。

translations.literal: Shu was ill and did not wish to cross the ranges; court deliberation also held that because he had merit he ought not be sent far out, and therefore he was moved to be Inspector of Xiangzhou; general, governor-general, and holding the tally remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu fell ill and was unwilling to cross the Nanling ridge into the far south; the court agreed that his past service should not be rewarded with banishment to a distant frontier, so he was reassigned as inspector of Xiangzhou while keeping his military titles and the credential tally.

sentences.zh: 征代鄧攸為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: He was summoned to replace Deng You as vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital to succeed Deng You as vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時將征蘇峻，司徒王導欲出舒為外援，乃授撫軍將軍、會稽內史，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: At the time they were about to campaign against Su Jun; Minister of Education Wang Dao wished to send Shu out as external support, and therefore invested him as General Who Pacifies the Army and Internal Secretary of Kuaiji, with salary rank of two thousand piculs at the middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: As preparations began for the expedition against Su Jun, Minister of Education Wang Dao wanted Wang Shu in the field as an outside bulwark, so he appointed him General Who Pacifies the Army and internal secretary of Kuaiji at the middle rank of two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 舒上疏辭以父名，朝議以字同音異，於禮無嫌。

translations.literal: Shu submitted a memorial declining on account of his father’s name; court deliberation held that although the characters were the same the sounds differed, and according to ritual there was no impropriety.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu memorialized that he could not take the post because the commandery name shared a character with his late father’s personal name; the court ruled that homophonous but differently pronounced taboos were not barred by ritual, so the objection did not stand.

sentences.zh: 舒復陳音雖異而字同，求換他郡。

translations.literal: Shu again stated that although the sounds differed the character was the same, and requested to be exchanged to another commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu pressed his case: the pronunciation might differ, but the written character was identical, and he asked to be given a different assignment.

sentences.zh: 於是改「會」字為「鄶」。

translations.literal: Thereupon they changed the character "hui" to "kuai" (in the placename).
translations.idiomatic: The court therefore ordered the commandery name written with a homophonous substitute graph so that his father's taboo character would not appear in his title.

sentences.zh: 舒不得已而行。

translations.literal: Shu had no choice but to go.
translations.idiomatic: With that face-saving compromise, Wang Shu had no choice but to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 在郡二年而蘇峻作逆，乃假舒節都督，行揚州刺史事。

translations.literal: He was in the commandery two years when Su Jun rebelled; thereupon they lent Shu the tally and staff of command as governor-general and had him act in the affairs of the Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had governed Kuaiji for two years when Su Jun rose in rebellion; the court then vested him with the ceremonial credentials of area commander and put him in charge of Yangzhou as acting provincial inspector.

sentences.zh: 時吳國內史庾冰棄郡奔舒，舒移告屬縣，以吳王師虞為軍司，御史中丞謝藻行龍驤將軍、監前鋒征討軍事，率衆一萬，與庾冰俱渡浙江。

translations.literal: At that time Internal Secretary of the Wu princedom Yu Bing abandoned the commandery and fled to Shu; Shu shifted notices to the subordinate counties, appointing Wu wangshi Yu as army staff director, Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk Xie Zuo acting as General Who Soars like a Dragon and supervising vanguard punitive operations, leading a host of ten thousand, and together with Yu Bing crossed the Zhe River.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Bing, internal secretary of the Wu princedom, abandoned his post and fled to Wang Shu, Wang Shu issued orders to his counties, took Yu Tan of Wu Xing onto his staff as army director—the transmitted text is defective here, but parallel records identify Yu Tan as the officer appointed—and placed Xie Zuo, the imperial censor, in acting command as General Who Soars like a Dragon over the vanguard; with ten thousand men they crossed the Zhe River together with Yu Bing.

sentences.zh: 前義興太守顧衆、護軍參軍顧颺等，皆起義軍以應舒。

translations.literal: Former Administrator of Yixing Gu Zhong, adviser on the staff of the Guards General Gu Yang, and others all raised righteous armies to respond to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Former Yixing prefect Gu Zhong, Gu Yang of the guards general’s staff, and others each raised loyalist militias to answer Wang Shu’s call.

sentences.zh: 舒假衆揚威將軍、督護吳中軍事，颺監晉陵軍事，於禦亭築壘。

translations.literal: Shu lent Zhong the title General Who Displays Might and supervisor who protects military affairs in Wu; Yang supervised military affairs in Jinling; they built ramparts at Yuting.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu breveted Gu Zhong as General Who Displays Might with overall charge of operations in Wu, assigned Gu Yang to oversee the Jinling theater, and had them throw up fortifications at Yuting.

sentences.zh: 峻聞舒等兵起，乃赦庾亮諸弟，以悅東軍。

translations.literal: When Jun heard that Shu and the others’ troops had risen, he thereupon pardoned Yu Liang’s various younger brothers in order to please the eastern armies.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Wang Shu had taken the field, Su Jun issued a general amnesty for Yu Liang’s brothers, hoping to placate the loyalist forces in the east.

sentences.zh: 舒率衆次郡之西江，為冰、藻後繼。

translations.literal: Shu led the host and halted at the western river of the commandery, as rear support for Bing and Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu brought his army up to the western branch of the river in his commandery to cover Yu Bing and Xie Zuo as a second line.

sentences.zh: 冰、颺等遣前鋒進據無錫，遇賊將張健等數千人，交戰，大敗，奔還禦亭，復自相驚擾，冰、颺等並退于錢唐，藻守嘉興。

translations.literal: Bing, Yang, and others dispatched the vanguard to advance and occupy Wuxi; they encountered several thousand of the rebel generals Zhang Jian and others, joined battle, were greatly defeated, fled back to Yuting, again alarmed and disturbed one another, Bing and Yang and others together retreated to Qiantang, and Zuo guarded Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing, Gu Zhong, Gu Yang, and their colleagues pushed the vanguard toward Wuxi, collided with several thousand men under the rebel commander Zhang Jian, suffered a crushing defeat, and bolted for Yuting; in the panic they fell back in a body to Qiantang while Xie Zuo clung to Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 賊遂入吳，燒府舍，掠諸縣，所在塗地。

translations.literal: The rebels thereupon entered Wu, burned government buildings, plundered the various counties, and everywhere smeared the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then poured into Wu, torched yamen compounds, pillaged county after county, and left devastation wherever they passed.

sentences.zh: 舒以輕進奔敗，斬二軍主者，免冰、颺督護，以白衣行事。

translations.literal: Shu because of light advance and fleeing defeat beheaded the two who commanded the armies, removed Bing and Yang from supervisor who protects, and had them conduct affairs in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu blamed the reckless advance and rout: he executed the two unit commanders, stripped Yu Bing and Gu Yang of their supervisory posts, and left them to serve in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 更以顧衆督護吳晉陵軍，屯兵章埭。

translations.literal: He further appointed Gu Zhong supervisor who protects the armies of Wu and Jinling and stationed troops at Zhangdai.
translations.idiomatic: He reassigned Gu Zhong to coordinate the Wu and Jinling sectors and encamped troops at Zhangdai.

sentences.zh: 吳興太守虞潭率所領討健，屯烏苞亭，並不敢進。

translations.literal: Administrator of Wuxing Yu Tan led those he commanded to attack Jian, encamped at Wubaoting, and together did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan, prefect of Wuxing, marched against Zhang Jian with his own troops and halted at Wubaoting, but neither he nor his allies dared press the attack.

sentences.zh: 時暴雨大水，賊管商乘船旁出，襲潭及衆。

translations.literal: At that time there was violent rain and great flooding; the rebel Guan Shang took boats and went out on the side, attacking Tan and Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: A cloudburst sent floodwaters surging; the rebel Guan Shang slipped along side channels by boat and fell upon Yu Tan and Gu Zhong.

sentences.zh: 潭等奔敗。

translations.literal: Tan and the others fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan’s force broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 潭還保吳興，衆退守錢唐。

translations.literal: Tan returned and protected Wuxing; Zhong retreated and guarded Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan fell back to hold Wuxing while Gu Zhong withdrew into Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 舒更遣將軍陳孺率精銳千人增戍海浦，所在築壘。

translations.literal: Shu further dispatched General Chen Ru to lead a thousand picked troops to augment garrisons on the sea shore; everywhere they built ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu next sent General Chen Ru with a thousand picked men to reinforce the coastal posts and throw up palisades at each defile.

sentences.zh: 或勸舒宜還都，使謝藻守西陵，扶海立柵。

translations.literal: Someone urged Shu that he ought to return to the capital, have Xie Zuo guard Xiling, and along the sea erect palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Some advisers urged him to fall back toward the capital, leave Xie Zuo holding Xiling, and stake palisades along the seaward approaches.

sentences.zh: 舒不聽，留藻守錢唐，使衆、颺守紫壁。

translations.literal: Shu did not listen; he left Zuo to guard Qiantang, and had Zhong and Yang guard Zibi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu refused: he kept Xie Zuo at Qiantang and ordered Gu Zhong and Gu Yang to defend the Zibi line.

sentences.zh: 於是賊轉攻吳興，潭諸軍復退。

translations.literal: Thereupon the rebels turned to attack Wuxing; Tan’s various armies again retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then shifted their weight against Wuxing, and Yu Tan’s columns fell back once more.

sentences.zh: 賊復掠東遷、余杭、武康諸縣。

translations.literal: The rebels again plundered the counties Dongqian, Yuhang, and Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Dongqian, Yuhang, Wukang, and the other counties in turn.

sentences.zh: 舒遣子允之行揚烈將軍，與將軍徐遜、陳孺及揚烈司馬硃燾，以精銳三千，輕邀賊于武康，出其不意，遂破之，斬首數百級，賊悉委舟步走。

translations.literal: Shu dispatched his son Yunzhi to act as General Who Displays Fierce Valor, together with General Xu Xun, Chen Ru, and Major of the General Who Displays Fierce Valor Zhu Dao, with three thousand picked troops lightly to intercept the rebels at Wukang; coming out where they did not expect, they thereupon defeated them, beheaded several hundred grades, and the rebels all abandoned boats and went on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu sent his son Wang Yunzhi, acting as General Who Displays Fierce Valor, with Xu Xun, Chen Ru, and Zhu Dao, his major, leading three thousand picked troops on a lightning strike at Wukang; catching the enemy off guard, they shattered the rebel band, took several hundred heads, and drove Su Jun’s men to abandon their boats and flee overland.

sentences.zh: 允之收其器械，進兵助潭。

translations.literal: Yunzhi collected their weapons and tools, advanced troops, and aided Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yunzhi gathered the captured arms and pushed forward to reinforce Yu Tan.

sentences.zh: 時賊韓晃既破宣城，轉人故鄣、長城。

translations.literal: At that time the rebel Han Huang had already broken Xuancheng, turned, and entered Guzhang and Changcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the rebel commander Han Huang, having stormed Xuancheng, swung his column toward Guzhang and Changcheng.

sentences.zh: 允之遣硃燾、何准等於之，戰擊於湖。

translations.literal: Yunzhi dispatched Zhu Dao, He Zhun, and others against them; they battled and struck at Yu Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yunzhi sent Zhu Dao, He Zhun, and others to strike the enemy; the loyalists brought Han Huang to battle at Yu Lake, though the terse wording of the line has led commentators to suspect a small scribal slip in the received text.

sentences.zh: 潭以強弩射之，晃等退走，斬首千餘級，納降二千人。

translations.literal: Tan with strong crossbows shot them; Huang and others retreated and fled; they beheaded more than a thousand grades and admitted surrender of two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan raked the enemy with heavy crossbow fire until Han Huang broke off; the loyalists counted more than a thousand heads and enrolled two thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 潭由是得保郡。

translations.literal: Tan by this was able to protect the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That victory let Yu Tan hold his prefecture intact.

sentences.zh: 是時臨海、新安諸山縣並反應賊，舒分兵悉討平之。

translations.literal: At this time the various mountain counties of Linhai and Xinan together rebelled and responded to the rebels; Shu divided troops and entirely campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain districts in Linhai and Xinan rose in sympathy with the rebels; Wang Shu detached columns and pacified each pocket.

sentences.zh: 會陶侃等至京都，舒、潭等並以屢戰失利，移書盟府，自貶去節。

translations.literal: When Tao Kan and others reached the capital city, Shu, Tan, and others together because of repeated battles and losses sent letters to the alliance headquarters and demoted themselves by removing the tally.
translations.idiomatic: After Tao Kan’s host reached the capital, Wang Shu and Yu Tan—ashamed of their repeated defeats—wrote to the coalition command asking to be stripped of their ceremonial axes.

sentences.zh: 侃遣使敦喻，不聽。

translations.literal: Kan dispatched envoys earnestly to instruct them; they did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan sent messengers urging them to relent, but they would not withdraw their resignations.

sentences.zh: 及侃立行台，上舒監浙江東五郡軍事，允之督護吳郡、義興、晉陵三郡征討軍事。

translations.literal: When Kan established a mobile headquarters, he submitted that Shu supervise military affairs of the five commanderies east of the Zhe River, and Yunzhi supervise who protects punitive operations of the three commanderies Wu, Yixing, and Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tao Kan set up his field headquarters, he memorialized that Wang Shu oversee the five commanderies east of the Zhe and that Wang Yunzhi coordinate the expeditionary forces of Wu, Yixing, and Jinling.

sentences.zh: 既而晃等南走，允之追躡於長塘湖，復大破之。

translations.literal: Before long Huang and others fled south; Yunzhi pursued their tracks at Changtang Lake and again greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang then bolted south; Wang Yunzhi ran him down at Changtang Lake and shattered his column a second time.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以功封彭澤縣侯，尋卒官，贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, by merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Pengze County; before long he died in office; he was posthumously awarded General-in-Chief of Chariots and Cavalry, ceremony equal to the Three Offices, and his posthumous name was Mu.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion he was ennobled as marquis of Pengze county for his service; he died in office soon afterward and was posthumously honored as general-in-chief of chariots and cavalry with rites matching the Three Dukes; his temple name-style posthumous title was Mu, “Solemn.”

sentences.zh: 長子晏之，蘇峻時為護軍參軍，被害。

translations.literal: The eldest son Yanzi, at the time of Su Jun, was adviser on the staff of the Guards General and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son, Wang Yanzi, was serving as an aide on the guards general’s staff when Su Jun’s coup claimed his life.

sentences.zh: 晏之子崐之嗣。

translations.literal: Yanzi’s son Kunzhi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed to Wang Yanzi’s son Wang Kunzhi.

sentences.zh: 卒，子陋之嗣。

translations.literal: He died; son Louzhi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Wang Louzhi succeeded to the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 宋受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Song received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu founded the Song and received the Jin abdication, the marquisate was abolished.

sentences.zh: 晏之弟允之最知名。

translations.literal: Yanzi’s younger brother Yunzhi was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Among Wang Yanzi’s brothers, Wang Yunzhi became by far the most celebrated.

translations.literal: The chapter text here records only an equals sign, a layout marker carried over from the digitized source.

sentences.zh: 子允之

translations.literal: Son Yunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Yunzhi

sentences.zh: =允之字深猷。

translations.literal: = Yunzhi’s courtesy name was Shenyou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yunzhi’s courtesy name was Shenyou.

sentences.zh: 總角，從伯敦謂為似己，恆以自隨，出則同輿，入則共寢。

translations.literal: From the hair-braiding age, his uncle Dun said he resembled himself, always took him along following himself, when going out then shared the same carriage, when entering then slept together.
translations.idiomatic: While still a boy he so reminded his uncle Wang Dun of himself that Dun never traveled without him: they rode in the same carriage and even shared a couch at night.

sentences.zh: 敦嘗夜飲，允之辭醉先臥。

translations.literal: Dun once drank at night; Yunzhi declined being drunk, first lay down.
translations.idiomatic: Once, during one of Wang Dun’s midnight drinking bouts, Wang Yunzhi pleaded drunkenness and turned in early.

sentences.zh: 敦與錢鳳謀為逆，允之已醒，悉聞其言，慮敦或疑己，便於臥處大吐，衣面並汙。

translations.literal: Dun with Qian Feng plotted to rebel; Yunzhi was already awake, fully heard their words, worried that Dun might suspect himself, then at the place where he lay vomited greatly, and clothes and face together were soiled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun and Qian Feng began plotting treason while Wang Yunzhi lay awake, hearing every word; fearing suspicion, he rolled from his couch and pretended a bout of violent vomiting until his robe and face were filthy.

sentences.zh: 鳳既出，敦果照視，見允之臥吐中，以為大醉，不復疑之。

translations.literal: When Feng had gone out, Dun indeed illuminated and looked, saw Yunzhi lying in vomit, thought him greatly drunk, and no longer suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: After Qian Feng left, Wang Dun brought a lamp to his nephew’s bedside, saw him sprawled in vomit, assumed he was dead drunk, and dropped his suspicions.

sentences.zh: 時父舒始拜廷尉，允之求還定省，敦許之。

translations.literal: At that time his father Shu had just been appointed Minister of Justice; Yunzhi requested to return to attend and inquire; Dun permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Wang Shu had been named minister of justice, so Wang Yunzhi asked leave to visit his parents; Wang Dun consented.

sentences.zh: 至都，以敦、鳳謀議事白舒，舒即與導俱啟明帝。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, he reported to Shu the matters of Dun and Feng’s plotting; Shu immediately together with Dao jointly informed Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the capital he told his father everything he had overheard of Wang Dun’s and Qian Feng’s plot; Wang Shu went straight to Wang Dao, and together they laid the matter before Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 舒為荊州，允之隨在西府。

translations.literal: When Shu was in Jingzhou, Yunzhi followed in the western headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shu took up the Jingzhou command, Wang Yunzhi joined him at the western headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及敦平，帝欲令允之仕，舒請曰：「臣子尚少，不樂早官。

translations.literal: When Dun was pacified, the emperor wished to order Yunzhi to take office; Shu requested, saying, “My son is still young and does not delight in early office.”
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun’s rebellion collapsed, Emperor Ming wanted to place Wang Yunzhi in office, but Wang Shu pleaded, “The boy is still young; I would rather not rush him into a career.”

sentences.zh: 」帝許隨舒之會稽。

translations.literal: The emperor permitted him to follow Shu to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor allowed him to accompany his father to Kuaiji instead.

sentences.zh: 及蘇峻反，允之討賊有功，封番禺縣侯，邑千六百戶，除建武將軍、錢唐令，領司鹽都尉。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, Yunzhi campaigned against the rebels and had merit; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Panyu County, fief of one thousand six hundred households, was appointed General Who Establishes Might, Magistrate of Qiantang, and concurrently Colonel Director of Salt.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Jun’s revolt Wang Yunzhi distinguished himself in the field and was ennobled as marquis of Panyu with sixteen hundred households; he was named General Who Establishes Might, magistrate of Qiantang, and salt intendant for the circuit.

sentences.zh: 舒卒，去職。

translations.literal: When Shu died, he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned his posts when his father died.

sentences.zh: 既葬，除義興太守，以憂哀不拜，從伯導與其書曰：「太保、安豐侯以孝聞天下，不得辭司隸；

translations.literal: After burial, he was appointed Administrator of Yixing; because of grief and sorrow he did not assume office; his uncle Dao wrote him a letter, saying, “The grand guardian, Marquis of Anfeng, by filial piety was heard of in the realm; he could not decline the Metropolitan Commandant.”
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral he was named prefect of Yixing but, crushed by mourning, refused to take up the seal; his uncle Wang Dao wrote, “Grand Guardian He Zeng, Marquis of Anfeng, was famed empire-wide for filial devotion, yet even he could not refuse appointment as metropolitan commandant.”

sentences.zh: 和長輿海內名士，不免作中書令。

translations.literal: He Changyu, famous scholar within the seas, did not avoid becoming Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He Qiao, whose courtesy name was Changyu and who was accounted a leading scholar of the age, still had to accept the post of palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 吾群從死亡略盡，子弟零落，遇汝如親，如其不爾，吾復何言！

translations.literal: Our group of cousins by death are nearly exhausted, sons and younger brothers scattered and fallen; meeting you is like kin—if it were not thus, what more would I say!
translations.idiomatic: “Our cousins have been all but wiped out, and the younger generation is scattered; to me you are as close as a son—if you will not heed me, I have nothing left to say.”

sentences.zh: 」允之固不肯就。

translations.literal: Yunzhi firmly was unwilling to go to it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yunzhi still would not accept the post.

sentences.zh: 咸和末，除宣城內史、監揚州江西四郡事、建武將軍，鎮於湖。

translations.literal: At the end of Xianhe, he was appointed Internal Secretary of Xuancheng, supervised affairs of the four commanderies of Yangzhou west of the river, General Who Establishes Might, and garrisoned Yu Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xianhe era he became internal secretary of Xuancheng, military overseer of the four Jiangxi commanderies in Yangzhou, and General Who Establishes Might, with headquarters at Yu Lake.

sentences.zh: 咸康中，進號西中郎將、假節。

translations.literal: In the middle of Xiankang, he advanced in title to General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the West and was given the tally.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiankang his rank was raised to General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the West with credential authority.

sentences.zh: 尋遷南中郎將、江州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the South and inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 蒞政甚有威惠。

translations.literal: In attending to government he had very much awe and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: His administration combined firm authority with genuine generosity.

sentences.zh: 時王恬服闋，除豫章郡。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Tian’s mourning clothes were ended; he was appointed to Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: About the time Wang Tian came off mourning for his father, the court named him administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 允之聞之驚愕，以為恬丞相子，應被優遇，不可出為遠郡，乃求自解州，欲與庾冰言之。

translations.literal: When Yunzhi heard it he was startled; he thought Tian was the chancellor’s son, ought to receive preferential treatment, could not be sent out as a distant commandery, and therefore sought himself to dissolve the province, wishing to speak of it to Yu Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yunzhi was stunned: Wang Tian was the grand chancellor’s son, he thought, and deserved preferential treatment, not exile to a remote commandery; he offered to surrender his own provincial post so he could remonstrate with Yu Bing.

sentences.zh: 冰聞甚愧，即以恬為吳郡，而以允之為衛將軍、會稽內史。

translations.literal: When Bing heard, he was very ashamed; thereupon he made Tian Wu commandery, and made Yunzhi General Who Guards the Army and Internal Secretary of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Mortified, Yu Bing reassigned Wang Tian to wealthy Wu commandery and instead named Wang Yunzhi General Who Guards the Army and internal secretary of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 未到，卒，年四十。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, he died, age forty.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the road before reaching his new post, aged forty.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous epithet was Zhong, “Loyal.”

sentences.zh: 子晞之嗣。

translations.literal: Son Xizhi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Xizhi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 卒，子肇之嗣。

translations.literal: He died; son Zhaozhi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Wang Zhaozhi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 王廙

translations.literal: Wang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi

sentences.zh: 王廙，字世將，丞相導從弟，而元帝姨弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Yi, courtesy name Shijiang, was Chancellor Dao’s younger male cousin, and moreover was Emperor Yuan’s younger maternal-cousin brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, courtesy name Shijiang, was a cousin of Grand Chancellor Wang Dao and, on his mother’s side, a younger cousin of Emperor Yuan of Jin.

sentences.zh: 父正，尚書郎。

translations.literal: His father was Wang Zheng, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Wang Zheng, had served as a gentleman in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 廙少能屬文，多所通涉，工書畫，善音樂、射御、博弈、雜伎。

translations.literal: In his youth Yi was able to compose texts, broadly penetrated many subjects, was skilled in calligraphy and painting, was good at music, archery and charioteering, board games, and miscellaneous arts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi showed literary talent early, read widely, excelled at painting and calligraphy, and mastered music, archery, horsemanship, chess, and every sort of polite accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 辟太傅掾，轉參軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as retainer of the grand tutor, transferred to be adviser on the staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited to the grand tutor’s secretariat, then moved onto a general’s staff as military adviser.

sentences.zh: 豫迎大駕，封武陵縣侯，拜尚書郎，出為濮陽太守。

translations.literal: He participated in welcoming the great chariot, was enfeoffed Marquis of Wuling County, was appointed Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, went out and became Administrator of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in welcoming Emperor Min’s court to the east, was ennobled as marquis of Wuling county, rose to gentleman in the Department of State Affairs, and was then posted out as prefect of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 元帝作鎮江左，廙棄郡過江。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan established headquarters on the left of the river, Yi abandoned the commandery and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Rui began building his power south of the Yangzi, Wang Yi resigned his prefecture and crossed the river to join him.

sentences.zh: 帝見之大悅，以為司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor saw him and was greatly pleased, appointing him marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign took an instant liking to him and named him marshal of his staff.

sentences.zh: 頻守廬江、鄱陽二郡。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he guarded the two commanderies Lujiang and Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: He successively held the defense of Lujiang and Poyang.

sentences.zh: 豫討周馥、杜韜，以功累增封邑，除冠軍將軍，鎮石頭，領丞相軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: He participated in punishing Zhou Fu and Du Tao; by merit his fief was repeatedly increased; he was appointed General Who Crowns the Army, garrisoned Stone Citadel, and concurrently libationer-adviser on the chancellor’s staff.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the campaigns against Zhou Fu and Du Tao, earned repeated enlargements of his fief, became General Who Crowns the Army with command at Stone Citadel, and joined the chancellor’s staff as libationer-adviser.

sentences.zh: 王敦啟為甯遠將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Dun memorialized that he be made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun petitioned the court to appoint him General Who Pacifies the Distance and inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，廙奏《中興賦》，上疏曰：

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, Yi presented the “Rhapsody on the Restoration” and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yuan took the throne, Wang Yi presented his “Rhapsody on the Restoration” and laid before the throne a memorial that began:

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: The text is long and is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ran too long to be copied into this history.

sentences.zh: 初，王敦左遷陶侃，使廙代為荊州。

translations.literal: At first, when Wang Dun demoted Tao Kan and had Yi replace him in Jingzhou,
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Dun had Tao Kan cashiered and sent Wang Yi to Jingzhou in his stead,

sentences.zh: 將吏馬俊、鄭攀等上書請留侃，敦不許。

translations.literal: the officers Ma Jun, Zheng Pan, and others submitted memorials asking to retain Kan; Dun did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: staff officers Ma Jun and Zheng Pan petitioned to keep Tao Kan in place, but Wang Dun refused.

sentences.zh: 廙為俊等所襲，奔于江安。

translations.literal: Yi was attacked by Jun and the others and fled to Jiang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi was ambushed by Ma Jun’s faction and fled downriver to Jiang’an.

sentences.zh: 賊杜曾與俊、攀北迎第五猗以距廙。

translations.literal: The rebel Du Zeng with Jun and Pan went north to welcome the Fifth Yi to resist Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Du Zeng joined Ma Jun and Zheng Pan in marching north to escort Fifth Yi into the field against Wang Yi.

sentences.zh: 廙督諸軍討曾，又為曾所敗。

translations.literal: Yi supervised the various armies to punish Zeng, and again was defeated by Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi led government troops against Du Zeng and was beaten again.

sentences.zh: 敦命湘州刺史甘卓、豫章太守周廣等助廙擊曾，曾衆潰，廙得到州。

translations.literal: Dun ordered Inspector of Xiangzhou Gan Zhuo, Administrator of Yuzhang Zhou Guang, and others to assist Yi in striking Zeng; Zeng’s host was routed, and Yi was able to reach the province.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun ordered Gan Zhuo of Xiangzhou, Zhou Guang of Yuzhang, and others to reinforce Wang Yi; Du Zeng’s army collapsed, and Wang Yi at last entered his provincial seat.

sentences.zh: 廙性俊率，嘗從南下，旦自尋陽，迅風飛帆，暮至都，倚舫樓長嘯，神氣甚逸。

translations.literal: Yi’s nature was handsome and frank; once when traveling south from dawn at Xunyang with swift wind flying sails, at evening he reached the capital; leaning on the upper deck of the boat he gave a long whistle, his spirit bearing very easeful.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi was dashing and outspoken: sailing south from Xunyang under a favoring gale, he reached the capital the same evening, leaned on the cabin rail, and let out a long whistle, utterly at ease.

sentences.zh: 王導謂庾亮曰：「世將為傷時識事。

translations.literal: Wang Dao said to Yu Liang, “Shijiang is one wounded by the times in discerning affairs.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao remarked to Yu Liang, “Shijiang is the sort of man the age has scarred yet taught to read events keenly.”

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「正足舒其逸氣耳。

translations.literal: Liang said, “It only suffices to vent his unruly spirit.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang replied, “Then let him blow off that restless temper.”

sentences.zh: 」廙在州大誅戮侃時將佐，及征士皇甫方回，於是大失荊土之望，人情乖阻。

translations.literal: Yi in the province greatly executed and slaughtered Kan’s former officers and the summoned scholar Huangfu Fanghui; thereby he greatly lost the hopes of the Jingzhou gentry, and human feelings turned contrary and obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingzhou Wang Yi carried out wholesale executions among Tao Kan’s old subordinates and even killed the recluse-scholar Huangfu Fanghui; he forfeited the goodwill of the local elite and alienated popular sentiment.

sentences.zh: 帝乃征廙為輔國將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon summoned Yi to be General Who Supports the State, with additional title Cavalry-in-Attendance Without Specification.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled him as General Who Supports the State with the added honorific of cavalry attendant-at-large.

sentences.zh: 以母喪去職。

translations.literal: Because of his mother’s death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，拜征虜將軍，進左衛將軍。

translations.literal: When mourning clothes were ended, he was appointed General Who Captures Caitiffs and advanced to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning term ended he was named General Who Captures Caitiffs and soon promoted to general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 及王敦構禍，帝遣廙喻敦，既不能諫其悖逆，乃為敦所留，受任助亂。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun brought disaster, the emperor dispatched Yi to instruct Dun; he was neither able to remonstrate against Dun’s rebellion, and thereupon was detained by Dun, received appointment, and assisted the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rose against the throne, Emperor Yuan sent Wang Yi to talk him down; Wang Yi neither dissuaded him nor broke free, stayed under duress, and took office on the rebel side.

sentences.zh: 敦得志，以廙為平南將領護南蠻校尉、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: When Dun achieved his aims, he appointed Yi General Who Pacifies the South, concurrently Colonel of the Southern Man, and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the coup Wang Dun made him General Who Pacifies the South, colonel of the Southern Man, and inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋病卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 帝猶以親故，深痛湣之。

translations.literal: The emperor still because of kinship was deeply pained and grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, remembering the family tie, mourned him with uncommon grief.

sentences.zh: 喪還京都，皇太子親臨拜柩，如家人之禮。

translations.literal: When the coffin returned to the capital city, the crown prince in person came to bow to the bier, with rites like those of family members.
translations.idiomatic: As the hearse entered the capital, the heir apparent personally paid his respects at the bier as though mourning a kinsman.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、驃騎將軍，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as palace attendant and general of agile cavalry; his posthumous epithet was Kang, “Peaceful.”

sentences.zh: 明帝與大將軍溫嶠書曰：「痛謝鯤未絕於口，世將復至於此。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, in a letter to Grand General Wen Jiao, said, “The pain of Xie Kun is not yet gone from my mouth, and Shijiang has again come to this.”
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming wrote to Wen Jiao, “I still ache whenever I speak of Xie Kun, and now Shijiang has met the same fate.”

sentences.zh: 並盛年雋才，不遂其志，痛切於心。

translations.literal: Together in the prime of life with outstanding talent, they did not realize their aims; the pain cuts to the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Both were brilliant men cut off in their prime; the loss cuts deep.

sentences.zh: 廙明古多通，鯤遠有識致。

translations.literal: Yi understood antiquity and was broadly learned; Kun had far-reaching insight and taste.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi was steeped in the classics and encyclopedic; Xie Kun had a discerning mind and rare judgment.

sentences.zh: 其言雖未足令人改聽，然味之不倦，近未易有也。

translations.literal: Their words although not sufficient to make people change what they hear, yet savoring them one is not weary—lately there is nothing easy to match them.
translations.idiomatic: Their conversation might not overturn every prejudice, yet one could listen forever; in our own day few men rival them.

sentences.zh: 坐相視盡，如何！」

translations.literal: Sitting, we have looked at each other to exhaustion—how can it be!”
translations.idiomatic: We have stared at one another until words fail—what more is there to say!”

sentences.zh: 子頤之嗣，仕至東海內史。

translations.literal: Son Yizhi inherited; in office he reached Internal Secretary of the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Yizhi succeeded him and rose to be internal secretary of the Eastern Sea princedom.

sentences.zh: 頤之弟胡之，字修齡，弱冠有聲譽，歷郡守、侍中、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Yizhi’s younger brother Huzhi, courtesy name Xiuling, at the capping age had a reputation; he passed through commandery governor, palace attendant, and chief of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yizhi’s brother Wang Huzhi, courtesy name Xiuling, was already celebrated when he came of age and served successively as prefect, palace attendant, and governor of the capital county.

sentences.zh: 素有風眩疾，發動甚數，而神明不損。

translations.literal: From of old he had wind-vertigo illness; the attacks were very frequent, yet his spirit intelligence was not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: He had long suffered crippling spells of vertigo, yet his mind stayed perfectly clear between attacks.

sentences.zh: 石季龍死，朝廷欲綏輯河洛，以胡之為西中郎將、司州刺史、假節，以疾固辭，未行而卒。

translations.literal: When Shi Jilong died, the court wished to pacify and gather He and Luo; they appointed Huzhi General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the West, Inspector of Sizhou, and lent him the tally; because of illness he firmly declined, had not yet gone, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Hu’s death the court planned to recover the central plains and named Wang Huzhi General of the Gentlemen of the Household of the West and inspector of Sizhou with credential authority; ill health forced him to decline before he could take up the post, and he died.

sentences.zh: 子茂之亦有美譽，官至晉陵太守。

translations.literal: Son Maozhi also had a fine reputation; in office he reached Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Maozhi likewise enjoyed a fine name and became prefect of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 子敬弘，義熙末為尚書。

translations.literal: Son Jinghong, at the end of Yixi, was Minister.
translations.idiomatic: A later descendant, Wang Jinghong, served as a minister at the close of the Yixi era.

translations.literal: The chapter text records only an equals sign, a layout marker from the digitized source.

sentences.zh: 弟彬

translations.literal: Younger brother Bin.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wang Bin

sentences.zh: =彬字世儒。

translations.literal: = Bin’s courtesy name was Shiru.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin’s courtesy name was Shiru.

sentences.zh: 少稱雅正，弱冠，不就州郡之命。

translations.literal: In his youth he was called elegant and upright; at the capping age he did not accept summons from the province or commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he was praised for integrity; after his capping ceremony he ignored every provincial and local summons.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫傅祗辟為掾。

translations.literal: Superintendent of the Household Fu Zhi summoned him as retainer.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi, superintendent of the household, recruited him to his secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後與兄廙俱渡江，為揚州刺史劉機建武長史。

translations.literal: Later he crossed the river together with his elder brother Yi and became chief clerk of the Establishing Might army for Inspector of Yangzhou Liu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He later crossed the Yangzi with Wang Yi and joined Liu Ji’s staff in Yangzhou as chief clerk of the Establishing Might army.

sentences.zh: 元帝引為鎮東賊曹參軍，轉典兵參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan appointed him bandit-suppressing aide on the staff of the general who garrisoned the east, transferred to aide in charge of troops.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan named him bandit-suppressing aide on the eastern headquarters staff, then shifted him to troop adjutant.

sentences.zh: 豫討華軼功，封都亭侯，湣帝召為尚書郎，以道險不就。

translations.literal: By merit in participating in punishing Hua Yi he was enfeoffed Marquis of the Metropolitan Village; Emperor Min summoned him as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; because the roads were perilous he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He earned the duting marquisate for his part in crushing Hua Yi; Emperor Min called him to the capital as a gentleman of the masters of writing, but dangerous roads kept him from answering.

sentences.zh: 遷建安太守，徙義興內史，未之職，轉軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: He was transferred Administrator of Jian’an, moved to Internal Secretary of Yixing, had not yet gone to office, and was transferred libationer-adviser on the staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was slated for Jian’an and then Yixing, but before he could assume either post he was reassigned as army libationer-adviser.

sentences.zh: 中興建，稍遷侍中。

translations.literal: When the restoration was founded, he was gradually promoted to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south he rose step by step to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 從兄敦舉兵石頭，帝使彬勞之。

translations.literal: When his older cousin Dun raised troops at Stone Citadel, the emperor had Bin go to console him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun seized Stone Citadel, the emperor sent Wang Bin to offer him formal condolences.

sentences.zh: 會周顗遇害，彬素與顗善，先往哭顗，甚慟。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhou Yi had been killed; Bin from of old was on good terms with Yi, and first went to weep for Yi, very mournful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi had just been executed; Wang Bin, who had long been his friend, went first to mourn him and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 既而見敦，敦怪其有慘容，而問其所以。

translations.literal: Presently he saw Dun; Dun wondered that he had a grief-stricken countenance and asked the reason thereof.
translations.idiomatic: When he then appeared before Wang Dun, Dun noticed his stricken face and demanded an explanation.

sentences.zh: 彬曰：「向哭伯仁，情未能已。

translations.literal: Bin said, “A moment ago I wept for Bozhou; the feeling could not yet cease.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin said, “I was weeping for Zhou Yi a moment ago; the grief will not leave me.”

sentences.zh: 」敦怒曰：「伯仁自致刑戮，且凡人遇汝，復何為者哉！

translations.literal: Dun angrily said, “Bozhou brought execution on himself; moreover, when ordinary men meet you, what do they do!”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun snarled, “Zhou Yi courted his own death—and what business is it of yours?”

sentences.zh: 」彬曰：「伯仁長者，君之親友，在朝雖無謇諤，亦非阿黨，而赦後加以極刑，所以傷惋也。

translations.literal: Bin said, “Bozhou was a senior man, your intimate friend; although in court he lacked blunt remonstrance, neither was he partisan; yet after the amnesty he was subjected to the extreme punishment—therefore I grieve and lament.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin answered, “Zhou Yi was your elder friend; he may not have spoken boldly at court, but he was no toady; to kill him even after the general amnesty is what wrings my heart.”

sentences.zh: 」因勃然數敦曰：「兄抗旌犯順，殺戮忠良，謀圖不軌，禍及門戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon in a burst of anger he counted Dun, saying, “Elder brother, you raise banners and violate the right, slaughter the loyal and good, plot unprincipled designs, and disaster reaches the gates and household.”
translations.idiomatic: He flared up and rebuked Wang Dun: “You march under rebel colors, butcher honest ministers, plot usurpation, and bring ruin on the whole clan.”

sentences.zh: 」音辭慷慨，聲淚俱下。

translations.literal: His tone and words were impassioned; sound and tears both descended.
translations.idiomatic: His voice shook with fury and tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 敦大怒，厲聲曰：「爾狂悖乃可至此，為吾不能殺汝邪！

translations.literal: Dun was greatly angry and in a stern voice said, “You are wild and contrary to the point of this—do you think I cannot kill you!”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun roared, “You dare defy me like this—do you imagine I cannot cut you down?”

sentences.zh: 」時王導在坐，為之懼，勸彬起謝。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Dao was seated there; for him it was fearful; he urged Bin to rise and apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao, who was present, was terrified and begged Wang Bin to rise and apologize.

sentences.zh: 彬曰：「有腳疾已來，見天子尚欲不拜，何跪之有！

translations.literal: Bin said, “Since the foot ailment came on, even seeing the Son of Heaven I still wish not to bow—what bowing is there!”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin retorted, “Ever since my leg trouble began I have refused to kneel even to the emperor—why should I kneel to Wang Dun?”

sentences.zh: 此復何所謝！

translations.literal: What moreover is there here to apologize for!”
translations.idiomatic: And what in the world would I be apologizing for?”

sentences.zh: 」敦曰：「腳痛孰若頸痛？

translations.literal: Dun said, “Does foot pain compare to neck pain?”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun sneered, “A sore foot is nothing beside a slit throat.”

sentences.zh: 」彬意氣自若，殊無懼容。

translations.literal: Bin’s bearing was as before; he had absolutely no fearful countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin’s composure never wavered; not a trace of fear showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 後敦議舉兵向京師，彬諫甚苦。

translations.literal: Later when Dun deliberated on raising troops toward the capital, Bin remonstrated very bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wang Dun plotted another march on the capital, Wang Bin argued against it with bitter earnestness.

sentences.zh: 敦變色目左右，將收彬，彬正色曰：「君昔歲害兄，今又殺弟邪？

translations.literal: Dun changed color and eyed those left and right, about to seize Bin; Bin in a stern voice said, “In former years you harmed an elder brother; now again you kill a younger brother?”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun’s face darkened and he signaled his guards to seize him; Wang Bin said coldly, “You murdered one brother years ago—will you kill another now?”

sentences.zh: 」先是，彬從兄豫章太守棱為敦所害，敦以彬親故容忍之。

translations.literal: Before this, Bin’s older cousin Administrator of Yuzhang Ling had been killed by Dun; because Bin was kin Dun on account of intimacy tolerated him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Dun had executed Wang Bin’s cousin Wang Ling, prefect of Yuzhang; only family feeling had kept Dun from harming Wang Bin himself.

sentences.zh: 俄而以彬為豫章太守。

translations.literal: Before long he appointed Bin Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wang Dun named him prefect of Yuzhang—perhaps to placate him.

sentences.zh: 彬為人樸素方直，乏風味之好，雖居顯貴，常布衣蔬食。

translations.literal: Bin as a person was plain, upright, and square; he lacked fondness for flavor and polish; although he occupied high honor, he always wore plain cloth and ate coarse vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin was plain, blunt, and frugal, with no taste for display; even at the summit of rank he dressed in homespun and ate simple fare.

sentences.zh: 遷前將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred General of the Front and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to General of the Front and inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及敦死，王含欲投王舒，王應勸含投彬。

translations.literal: When Dun died, Wang Han wished to throw himself on Wang Shu; Wang Ying urged Han to throw himself on Bin.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun’s death Wang Han wanted to flee to Wang Shu, but Wang Ying urged him to seek Wang Bin instead.

sentences.zh: 含曰：「大將軍平素與江州云何，汝欲歸之？

translations.literal: Han said, “The grand general on ordinary days with Jiangzhou—how was it; you wish to go to him?”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han asked, “Your father was never close to the Jiangzhou commander—why send us there?”

sentences.zh: 」應曰：「此乃所以宜往也。

translations.literal: Ying said, “This is exactly the reason it is fitting to go.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ying replied, “That is precisely why we should go.”

sentences.zh: 江州當人強盛時，能立同異，此非常人所及。

translations.literal: When Jiangzhou was in another’s strength and prosperity, he was able to set up agreement and difference; this is not what ordinary men reach.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangzhou commander was at the height of his power, he still dared defy the grand general—few ordinary men could do that.

sentences.zh: 睹衰厄，必興湣惻。

translations.literal: Seeing decline and distress, he is sure to raise pity.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing kinsmen now ruined, he is bound to pity us.

sentences.zh: 荊州守文，豈能意外行事！

translations.literal: Jingzhou guards the letter of the law—how can it act outside the pattern?
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou sticks to the rule book; it will never bend the rules for us.

sentences.zh: 」含不從，遂共投舒，舒果沈含父子于江。

translations.literal: Han did not follow; thereupon together they threw themselves on Shu, and Shu indeed drowned Han father and son in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Han refused, went to Wang Shu instead, and Wang Shu drowned father and son in the Yangzi as expected.

sentences.zh: 彬聞應來，密具船以待之。

translations.literal: When Bin heard that Ying was coming, he secretly prepared boats to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin, hearing that Wang Ying might come, quietly readied boats to receive them.

sentences.zh: 既不至，深以為恨。

translations.literal: When they did not arrive, he deeply took it as regret.
translations.idiomatic: When they never appeared, he felt bitter regret.

sentences.zh: 敦平，有司奏彬及兄子安成太守籍之，並是敦親，皆除名。

translations.literal: When Dun was pacified, the responsible officials memorialized that Bin and his elder brother’s son Administrator of Ancheng Jizhi together were Dun’s kin; all were removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion the ministry impeached Wang Bin and his nephew Wang Ji, prefect of Ancheng, as Wang Dun’s kinsmen and struck their names from office.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「司徒導以大義滅親，其後昆雖或有違，猶將百世宥之，況彬等公之近親。

translations.literal: An edict said, “Minister of Education Dao by great righteousness destroyed kin; although later descendants may sometimes have transgressed, still for a hundred generations they will be forgiven—how much more Bin and others are the duke’s close kin.”
translations.idiomatic: An edict answered, “Minister Wang Dao set duty above family; though later kin sometimes stumbled, the merit of his house should shield them for generations—let alone men as close as Wang Bin.”

sentences.zh: 」乃原之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne therefore quashed the impeachment.

sentences.zh: 徵拜光祿勳，轉度支尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Superintendent of the Household, transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as superintendent of the household, then promoted to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻平後，改築新宮，彬為大匠。

translations.literal: After Su Jun was pacified, they rebuilt the new palace; Bin was grand master builder.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun’s revolt the court rebuilt the palace complex, with Wang Bin as chief architect.

sentences.zh: 以營創勳勞，賜爵關內侯，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: By merit in camp founding and toil he was granted fief as Marquis Within the Passes, transferred Vice Director of the Secretariat on the right.
translations.idiomatic: For his labors in construction he received a marquisate within the passes and rose to vice director of the right of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年五十九。

translations.literal: He died in office, age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈特進、衛將軍，加散騎常侍，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded specially advanced, General Who Guards the Army, with additional Cavalry-in-Attendance Without Specification; posthumous name Su.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously advanced to specially advanced, general who guards the army, and cavalry attendant-at-large; his posthumous epithet was Su, “Stern.”

sentences.zh: 長子彭之嗣，位至黃門郎。

translations.literal: The eldest son Pengzhi inherited; in rank he reached Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Wang Pengzhi inherited the title and rose to gentleman at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 次彪之，最知名。

translations.literal: The second, Biao zhi, was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His second son, Wang Biao zhi, became the most celebrated of the line.

translations.literal: The chapter text records only an equals sign, a layout marker from the digitized source.

sentences.zh: 彬子彪之

translations.literal: Bin’s son Biao zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin’s son Wang Biao zhi

sentences.zh: =彪之字叔武。

translations.literal: = Biao zhi’s courtesy name was Shu wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi’s courtesy name was Shuwu.

sentences.zh: 年二十，須鬢皓白，時人謂之王白須。

translations.literal: At age twenty his beard and temples were hoary white; people of the time called him Wang Whitebeard.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty his beard and temples had already turned snowy white, and contemporaries nicknamed him “Lord White-Whiskers.”

sentences.zh: 初除佐著作郎、東海王文學。

translations.literal: At first removal he was appointed aide in editorial service and literary scholar to the Prince of the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointments were as editorial aide and tutor to the Prince of the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 從伯導謂曰：「選官欲以汝為尚書郎，汝幸可作諸王佐邪！

translations.literal: Uncle Dao said to him, “The selection office wishes to make you Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; are you content to be merely a prince’s adjutant!”
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Wang Dao teased him, “The personnel bureau wants you for gentleman of the masters of writing—would you really rather be a prince’s tutor?”

sentences.zh: 」彪之曰：「位之多少既不足計，自當任之于時，至於超遷，是所不願。

translations.literal: Biao zhi said, “That ranks are more or less is not worth calculating; naturally one should accept what the times assign; as for leap promotions, that is what I do not wish.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi answered, “Rank is not what matters; I will take whatever office the times offer, but I have no taste for sudden jumps up the ladder.”

sentences.zh: 」遂為郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon he became gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: So he took the gentleman post after all.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍將軍、武陵王晞以為司馬，累遷尚書左丞、司徒左長史、御史中丞、侍中、廷尉。

translations.literal: General Who Garrisons the Army, Prince of Wuling Xi, appointed him marshal; he was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Secretary on the left, chief clerk on the left of the Minister of Education, palace assistant imperial clerk, palace attendant, and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Garrisons the Army, Prince Sima Xi of Wuling, made him marshal; he climbed through supervising secretary, chief clerk of the minister of education, censor-in-chief, palace attendant, and minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 時永嘉太守謝毅。

translations.literal: At that time Yongjia Administrator Xie Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The affair began while Xie Yi was serving as prefect of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 赦後殺郡人周矯，矯從兄球詣州訴冤。

translations.literal: After the amnesty he killed a commandery man Zhou Jiao; Jiao’s older cousin by the father Qiu went to the province to lodge a grievance.
translations.idiomatic: After a general amnesty Xie Yi executed a local man named Zhou Jiao; Zhou’s cousin Zhou Qiu brought the case to the provincial yamen.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史殷浩遣從事疏收毅，付廷尉。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yangzhou Yin Hao dispatched an investigator to memorialize and seize Yi, delivering him to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao, inspector of Yangzhou, sent an investigator to arrest Xie Yi and remand him to the minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 彪之以球為獄主，身無王爵，非廷尉所料，不肯受，與州相反復。

translations.literal: Biao zhi held that Qiu was prison master; he himself lacked princely rank and was not what the Minister of Justice handles; he was unwilling to accept and with the province went back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi ruled that because Zhou Qiu acted as private prosecutor and held no noble title, the capital tribunal lacked jurisdiction; he refused the case and exchanged repeated protests with the province.

sentences.zh: 穆帝發詔令受之。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu issued an edict ordering him to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu issued a rescript ordering the minister of justice to take jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 彪之又上疏執據，時人比之張釋之。

translations.literal: Biao zhi again submitted a memorial holding fast to his grounds; people of the time compared him to Zhang Shizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi memorialized again, standing on statute law until the court yielded; contemporaries likened him to the Han jurist Zhang Shizhi.

sentences.zh: 時當南郊，簡文帝為撫軍，執政，訪彪之應有赦不。

translations.literal: At the time it was the southern suburban sacrifice; Emperor Jianwen was General Who Pacifies the Army, held power, and consulted Biao zhi whether there ought to be an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: As the court prepared the southern-suburb sacrifice, Emperor Jianwen—then regent as General Who Pacifies the Army—asked Wang Biao zhi whether a general amnesty should accompany the rite.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「中興以來，郊祀往往有赦，愚意嘗謂非宜。

translations.literal: He answered, saying, “Since the restoration, suburban sacrifices have often had amnesties; in my foolish opinion I have always held this unfitting.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi replied, “Ever since the court moved south, amnesties have routinely followed the suburban rites; in my humble view that practice is unwise.”

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 黎庶不達其意，將謂效祀必赦，至此時，凶愚之輩復生心於僥倖矣。

translations.literal: The common people do not grasp the intention; they will suppose that when the suburban sacrifice is performed there must be an amnesty; when this time comes, the fierce and foolish sort again give birth in their hearts to hopes of lucky chance.
translations.idiomatic: The people will misunderstand: they will assume every suburban sacrifice brings a blanket pardon, and on that day the vicious and the desperate will gamble on impunity once again.”

sentences.zh: 」遂從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 簡文有命用秣陵令曲安遠補句容令，殿中侍御史奚郎補湘東郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen had an order to use Moling Magistrate Qu Anyuan to fill Jurong, and Palace Attendant Censor Xi Lang to fill Xiangdong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen ordered Moling prefect Qu Anyuan transferred to Jurong and palace attendant censor Xi Lang posted to Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 彪之執不從，曰：「秣陵令三品縣耳，殿下昔用安遠，談者紛然。

translations.literal: Biao zhi held firm and did not follow, saying, “Moling is only a third-grade county; Your Highness once appointed Anyuan, and talkers were in an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi refused the edict, saying, “Moling is merely a third-rank county; when Your Highness last placed Qu Anyuan there, the court buzzed with criticism.”

sentences.zh: 句容近幾，三品佳邑，敢可處卜術之人無才用者邪！

translations.literal: Jurong is near the capital region, a fine third-grade county—how dare one place there men of divination arts without talent for use!
translations.idiomatic: Jurong sits on the capital’s doorstep—a prized third-rank seat. How can we park a fortune-teller with no administrative ability there?”

sentences.zh: 湘東雖復遠小，所用未有朗比，談者謂頗兼卜術得進。

translations.literal: Although Xiangdong is again remote and small, among appointees there has been none comparable to Lang; talkers say he advanced largely by combining divination arts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangdong may be remote, yet no previous nominee matched this Xi Lang; rumor already says he owes his rise to occult arts.

sentences.zh: 殿下若超用寒悴，當充人才可拔。

translations.literal: If Your Highness wishes to promote beyond the norm men of cold and humble station, you ought to fill the post with talent that can be raised.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness means to elevate men from cold families, choose someone whose talent justifies the leap.”

sentences.zh: 朗等凡器，實未足充此選。」

translations.literal: Lang and the like are ordinary vessels; truly they are not sufficient to fill this selection.”
translations.idiomatic: Xi Lang and his like are mediocrity; they cannot bear these appointments.”

sentences.zh: 太尉桓溫欲北伐，屢詔不許。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Huan Wen wished to campaign north; repeatedly edicts did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Huan Wen pressed for a northern expedition, but repeated edicts withheld approval.

sentences.zh: 溫輒下武昌，人情震懼。

translations.literal: Wen thereupon went down to Wuchang; human feelings trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen marched down to Wuchang anyway, and panic spread through the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 或勸殷浩引身告退，彪之言于簡文曰：「此非保社稷為殿下計，皆自為計耳。

translations.literal: Someone urged Yin Hao to withdraw his person and announce retirement; Biao zhi spoke to Emperor Jianwen, saying, “This is not planning to protect the altars of soil and grain for Your Highness; all are planning for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Some advisers told Yin Hao to resign; Wang Biao zhi said to Emperor Jianwen, “That counsel serves private careers, not the dynasty or Your Highness.”

sentences.zh: 若殷浩去職，人情崩駭，天子獨坐。

translations.literal: If Yin Hao leaves office, human feelings will collapse in terror, and the Son of Heaven will sit alone.
translations.idiomatic: If Yin Hao steps down, morale will shatter and the emperor will be left utterly isolated.”

sentences.zh: 既爾，當有任其責者，非殿下而誰！

translations.literal: Since it is so, there must be one who bears the responsibility—if not Your Highness, who!
translations.idiomatic: When that happens, someone must answer for it—and who but Your Highness?”

sentences.zh: 」又謂浩曰：「彼抗表問罪，卿為其首。

translations.literal: He further said to Hao, “He has submitted a memorial resisting and demanding punishment; you are its chief.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Yin Hao: “Huan Wen’s indictment names you first.”

sentences.zh: 事任如此，猜釁已構，欲作匹夫，豈有全地邪？

translations.literal: Affairs and responsibility being thus, suspicion and rift are already structured; wishing to be a common man—how can there be ground to remain whole!
translations.idiomatic: Matters stand at mutual suspicion; if you try to walk away a private citizen, do you imagine there is safe ground anywhere?”

sentences.zh: 且當靜以待之。

translations.literal: Moreover for the moment be still and await it.
translations.idiomatic: For now, stay calm and watch how the wind blows.”

sentences.zh: 令相王與手書，示以款誠，陳以成敗，當必旋旆。

translations.literal: Order the Prince of Langye to give a letter in his own hand, show sincerity, set forth success and failure, and he is sure to turn his banners.
translations.idiomatic: Have the Prince of Langye send a personal letter laying out sincerity and the stakes—Huan Wen will wheel his army about.”

sentences.zh: 若不順命，即遣中詔。

translations.literal: If he does not obey the command, then dispatch a palace edict.
translations.idiomatic: If he still defies you, issue an inner-court rescript.”

sentences.zh: 如復不奉，乃當以正義相裁。

translations.literal: If again he does not obey, then ought to use righteousness to judge him.
translations.idiomatic: If he ignores that as well, only then meet him with the full weight of legitimate authority.”

sentences.zh: ，無故匆匆，先自猖蹶。

translations.literal: , without cause in haste, first oneself wildly stumble.
translations.idiomatic: Above all, do not panic without cause and be the first to bring everything down.”

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「決大事正自難，頃日來欲使人悶，聞卿此謀，意始得了。

translations.literal: Hao said, “Deciding great affairs is indeed difficult; in recent days it has wanted to make people stifled; hearing this plan of yours, my mind at last attains clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao answered, “Great decisions are never easy; these days I have felt suffocated. Your plan finally clears my mind.”

sentences.zh: 」溫亦奉帝旨，果不進。

translations.literal: Wen also received the emperor’s order and indeed did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen likewise obeyed the imperial command and went no farther.

sentences.zh: 時衆官漸多，而遷徙每速，彪之上議曰：

translations.literal: At that time the host of officials gradually grew numerous, yet transfers were always rapid; Biao zhi submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: As offices multiplied and reshuffles accelerated, Wang Biao zhi laid before the throne a long memorial arguing that

sentences.zh: 為政之道，以得賢為急，非謂雍容廊廟，標的而已，固將蒞任贊時，職思其憂也。

translations.literal: The way of governing is to obtain the worthy as urgent; it does not mean merely to be at ease in the court hall as a target sign; indeed one will attend to office and aid the age, in duty pondering its worries.
translations.idiomatic: good government begins with securing worthy men—not with filling the ministry gallery like trophies on a wall, but with placing them in posts where they shoulder the age’s troubles.

sentences.zh: 得賢之道，在於蒞任；

translations.literal: The way to obtain the worthy lies in attending to office;
translations.idiomatic: Talent is secured by giving appointees real responsibility;

sentences.zh: 蒞任之道，在於能久；

translations.literal: the way to attend to office lies in being able to endure long;
translations.idiomatic: real responsibility requires that they be left in place long enough to matter;

sentences.zh: 久於其道，天下化成。

translations.literal: long in its way, the realm is transformed and completed.
translations.idiomatic: only long tenure lets the realm mature through their work.”

sentences.zh: 是以三載考績，三考黜陟，不收一切之功，不采速成之譽。

translations.literal: Therefore thrice yearly they examine merit, thrice examining they demote and promote; they do not gather all-at-once merit, they do not adopt reputations of sudden completion.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the classical triennial review and nine-year cycle—never promoting on a single burst of hype or a flash reputation.

sentences.zh: 故勳格辰極，道融四海，風流遐邈，聲冠百代。

translations.literal: Therefore merit matches the pole star, the Way permeates the four seas, influence flows far, and fame crowns a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: That is how true merit reaches the throne, the Way suffuses the empire, and a statesman’s name endures for ages.

sentences.zh: 凡庸之族衆，賢能之才寡，才寡於世而官多於朝，焉得不賢鄙共貫，清濁同官！

translations.literal: The clans of the mediocre are many, the talents of the worthy able are few; talents are few for the age yet offices are many at court—how can it not be that worthy and base share one string, clear and turbid share one office!
translations.idiomatic: Mediocrities swarm while genuine talent is scarce; with more chairs than capable men, the worthy and the worthless inevitably sit side by side, pure and foul mixed in the same ranks.”

sentences.zh: 官衆則闕多，闕多則遷速，前後去來，更相代補，非為故然，理固然耳。

translations.literal: When offices are many then vacancies are many; when vacancies are many then transfers are rapid; coming and going before and after, replacing one another in succession—this is not purposely thus, but principle is solidly thus.
translations.idiomatic: More posts mean more vacancies, more vacancies mean constant musical chairs—no malice required; the arithmetic of bureaucracy makes it inevitable.”

sentences.zh: 所以職事未修，朝風未澄者也。

translations.literal: This is why administrative tasks are not perfected and court custom is not clear.
translations.idiomatic: That is why business piles up unfinished and court discipline never clarifies.”

sentences.zh: 職事之修，在於省官；

translations.literal: The perfection of administrative tasks lies in reducing offices;
translations.idiomatic: To finish the work, trim redundant offices;

sentences.zh: 朝風之澄，在於並職。

translations.literal: the clarity of court custom lies in merging duties.
translations.idiomatic: to cleanse the court, merge overlapping portfolios.”

sentences.zh: 官省則選清而得久，職並則吏簡而俗靜；

translations.literal: When offices are reduced then selection is clear and one obtains endurance; when duties are merged then clerks are simplified and custom is quiet;
translations.idiomatic: Fewer bureaus yield cleaner appointments and longer tenure; merged duties mean leaner clerical staffs and calmer administration;

sentences.zh: 選清則勝人久於其事，事久則中才猶足有成。

translations.literal: when selection is clear then the winning man endures long in his task; when affairs are long then even middling talent still suffices to have accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: clear selection lets able men stay long enough to accomplish something—even middling talent matures with time.”

sentences.zh: 今內外百官，較而計之，固應有並省者矣。

translations.literal: Now inner and outer hundred officials, if compared and calculated, indeed ought to have those merged and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: A tally of capital and provincial posts shows where consolidation is overdue.”

sentences.zh: 六卿之任，太常望雅而職重，然其所司，義高務約。

translations.literal: Among the duties of the six ministers, the Grand Master of Ceremonies is lofty in repute yet heavy in duty, yet what it supervises, in principle is high and tasks are concise.
translations.idiomatic: The grand master of ceremonies bears august ritual duties yet his substantive workload is modest.”

sentences.zh: 宗正所統蓋鮮，可以並太常。

translations.literal: What the Director of the Imperial Clan governs is altogether scant; it can be merged with the Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the imperial clan has little to administer; merge it with the ritual ministry.”

sentences.zh: 宿衛之重，二衛任之，其次驍騎、左軍各有所領，無兵軍校皆應罷廢。

translations.literal: The weight of night guard lies with the two guards commands; next, Swift Cavalry and the Left Army each have what they lead; all military schools without troops ought to be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Palace security rests with the two guards commands and the swift-cavalry and left-army units; strip empty training cadres of their commissions.”

sentences.zh: 四軍皆罷，則左軍之名不宜獨立，宜改遊擊以對驍騎。

translations.literal: If the four armies are all abolished, then the name of the Left Army ought not stand alone; it should be changed to Roaming Attack to pair with Swift Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: If four hollow armies go, the left-army title should not stand alone—rename it Roaming Attack to balance Swift Cavalry.”

sentences.zh: 內官自侍中以下，舊員皆四，中興之初，二人而已。

translations.literal: Inner offices from attendant-in-chief downward, old complements were all four; at the beginning of the restoration, only two men.
translations.idiomatic: Palace posts from attendant-in-chief down once had four incumbents each; at the court’s southern landing only two remained.”

sentences.zh: 二人對直，或有不周，愚謂三人，於事則無闕也。

translations.literal: Two men pairing duty sometimes is not comprehensive; in my foolish opinion three men, for affairs then has no lack.
translations.idiomatic: Two men on rotating watch miss too much; three, I submit, cover the workload without waste.”

sentences.zh: 凡余諸官，無綜事實者，可令大官隨才位所帖而領之，若未能頓廢，自可因缺而省之。

translations.literal: As for the remaining various offices that lack comprehensive duties, one may order the great offices according to talent and rank to attach and oversee them; if they cannot be abolished at a stroke, naturally one may because of vacancies reduce them.
translations.idiomatic: Other sinecures can be folded into parent ministries by competence; where posts cannot vanish overnight, let attrition shrink them.”

sentences.zh: 委之以職分，責之以有成，能否因考績而著，清濁隨黜陟而彰。

translations.literal: Entrust them with division of duty, demand them with having accomplishment; ability and inability thereby appear in examination of merit, clear and turbid thereby manifest in demotion and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Define portfolios, demand results, and let triennial review separate able from useless, pure from corrupt.”
