sentences.zh: 雖緝熙之隆、康哉之歌未可，使庶官之選差清，蒞職之日差久，無奉祿之虛費，簡吏寺之煩役矣。

translations.literal: Although the splendor of “continuous brightness” and the song of “how peaceful” may not yet be attainable, still cause the selection of the many officials to be somewhat clearer, the days of attending office somewhat longer, have no empty waste of salary stipends, and reduce the vexing labor of clerical temples.
translations.idiomatic: We may never reach the golden age of the Book of Documents, yet we can still make appointments a little cleaner, tours of duty a little longer, stop paying idle salaries, and ease the clerks’ grind.”

sentences.zh: 永和末，多疾疫。

translations.literal: At the end of Yonghe, there were many epidemics.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yonghe era epidemics raged.

sentences.zh: 舊制，朝臣家有時疾，染易三人以上者，身雖無病，百日不得入宮。

translations.literal: By old regulation, if a court minister’s household had seasonal illness and infected three or more persons, although his person had no illness, for a hundred days he could not enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Old rules barred any minister whose household reported three contagious cases—even if he himself was well—from the palace for a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 至是，百官多列家疾，不入。

translations.literal: At this time, the hundred officials mostly listed household illness and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Officials now claimed sick families wholesale and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 彪之又言：「疾疫之年，家無不染。

translations.literal: Biao zhi again said, “In a year of epidemic, there is no household not infected.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi answered, “In a plague year every household falls ill.”

sentences.zh: 若以之不復人宮，則直侍頓闕，王者宮省空矣。

translations.literal: If by this one no longer enters the palace, then straight attendance suddenly lacks, and the king’s palace precincts are empty.
translations.idiomatic: If that keeps everyone out, the inner palaces lose every attendant and the sovereign sits in an empty court.”

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his argument.

sentences.zh: 既而長安人雷弱兒、梁安等詐云殺苻健、苻眉，請兵應接。

translations.literal: Before long men of Chang’an, Lei Ruo’er, Liang An, and others falsely said they had killed Fu Jian and Fu Mei and requested troops to link up.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chang’an adventurers Lei Ruo’er and Liang An falsely reported the deaths of Fu Jian and Fu Mei and begged reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 時殷浩鎮壽陽，便進據洛，營復山陵。

translations.literal: At that time Yin Hao garrisoned Shouyang, then advanced and occupied Luo, and campaigned to restore the mausoleums.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao, stationed at Shouyang, pushed toward Luoyang to reopen the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 屬彪之疾歸，上簡文帝箋，陳弱兒等容有詐偽，浩未應輕進。

translations.literal: It happened that Biao zhi was ill and returned; he submitted a note to Emperor Jianwen, stating that Ruo’er and the others might harbor fraud; Hao ought not lightly advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi, home on sick leave, sent Emperor Jianwen a confidential memo warning that Lei Ruo’er’s story was probably bogus and Yin Hao should not march rashly.

sentences.zh: 尋而弱兒果詐，姚襄反叛，浩大敗，退守譙城。

translations.literal: Before long Ruo’er indeed was fraudulent; Yao Xiang rebelled; Hao was greatly defeated and retreated to guard Qiao city.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Ruo’er’s tale collapsed, Yao Xiang mutinied, and Yin Hao’s army was routed back to Qiao.

sentences.zh: 簡文笑謂彪之曰：「果如君言。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen smiled and said to Biao zhi, “It indeed was as you said.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen smiled at Wang Biao zhi: “Events proved you right.”

sentences.zh: 自頃以來，君謀無遺策，張、陳何以過之！」

translations.literal: Since recent times, your plans have had no missed strategy; how could Zhang Liang and Chen Ping surpass this!”
translations.idiomatic: Lately none of your counsel has missed; even Zhang Liang and Chen Ping could not have done better!”

sentences.zh: 轉領軍將軍，遷尚書僕射，以疾病，不拜。

translations.literal: He was transferred General Who Leads the Army, promoted Vice Director of the Secretariat; because of illness he did not assume office.
translations.idiomatic: He was named general who leads the army and vice director of the Department of State Affairs, but illness kept him from taking up the latter post.

sentences.zh: 徙太常，領崇德衛尉。

translations.literal: He was moved to Grand Master of Ceremonies, concurrently Defender of Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to grand master of ceremonies while heading the Chongde guard command.

sentences.zh: 時或謂簡文曰：「武陵第中大修器杖，將謀非常也。

translations.literal: At that time someone said to Emperor Jianwen, “In the Prince of Wuling’s mansion they greatly repair weapons and gear; they will plot something extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Emperor Jianwen, “The Prince of Wuling is stockpiling arms—surely he plots treason.”

sentences.zh: 」簡文以彪之。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen consulted Biao zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Wang Biao zhi.

sentences.zh: 彪之曰：「武陵王志意盡于馳騁田獵耳。

translations.literal: Biao zhi said, “The Prince of Wuling’s ambition runs only to galloping and hunting fields and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi said, “His ambitions stop at hunting and the chase.”

sentences.zh: 願深靜之，以懷異同者。

translations.literal: I wish deeply to quiet it, in order to embrace those of different agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Let the matter drop quietly and you will reassure doubters.”

sentences.zh: 」或復以此為言，簡文甚悅。

translations.literal: Someone again spoke this as words; Emperor Jianwen was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the tale surfaced again, Emperor Jianwen was delighted with the answer.

sentences.zh: 復轉尚書僕射。

translations.literal: He was again transferred Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was again named vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時豫州刺史謝奕卒，簡文遽使彪之舉可以代奕者。

translations.literal: At that time Inspector of Yuzhou Xie Yi died; Emperor Jianwen hastily sent Biao zhi to raise who could replace Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuzhou inspector Xie Yi died, Emperor Jianwen urgently asked Wang Biao zhi whom to appoint.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「當今時賢，備簡高監。

translations.literal: He answered, saying, “The worthies of the present age are fully prepared in the high surveillance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi replied, “Today’s able men are already on file with the high personnel office.”

sentences.zh: 」簡文曰：「人有舉桓雲者，君謂如何？

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen said, “There is someone who raised Huan Yun; what do you say of it?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, “Someone suggests Huan Yun—your view?”

sentences.zh: 」彪之曰：「雲不必非才，然溫居上流，割天下之半。

translations.literal: Biao zhi said, “Yun need not lack talent, yet Wen occupies the upper river and has carved off half the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi said, “Huan Yun may be capable, but Huan Wen already controls the upper Yangzi and half the empire.”

sentences.zh: 其弟復處西籓，兵權盡出一門，亦非深根固蒂之宜也。

translations.literal: His younger brother again being stationed on the western screen, military authority entirely issues from one gate—this also is not what suits deep roots and firm base!
translations.idiomatic: Placing his brother on another great regional command concentrates military power in one clan—not how you deepen the dynasty’s roots.”

sentences.zh: 人才非可豫量，但當令不與殿下作異者耳。

translations.literal: Human talent cannot be measured in advance; but one ought to make it so that they do not oppose Your Highness—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Talent is hard to forecast—just be sure the nominee will not work against Your Highness.”

sentences.zh: 」簡文頷曰：「君言是也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen nodded, saying, “Your words are correct.”
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen nodded. “You are right.”

sentences.zh: 後以彪之為鎮軍將軍、會稽內史，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later they appointed Biao zhi General Who Garrisons the Army, Internal Secretary of Kuaiji, with additional Cavalry-in-Attendance Without Specification.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Biao zhi became General Who Garrisons the Army and internal secretary of Kuaiji, with the added honorific of cavalry attendant-at-large.

sentences.zh: 居郡八年，豪右斂跡，亡戶歸者三萬餘口。

translations.literal: He dwelt in the commandery eight years; the powerful families drew in their tracks; returned fugitive households were more than thirty thousand mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years in office cowed the magnates and brought back over thirty thousand registered taxpayers.

sentences.zh: 桓溫下鎮姑孰，威勢震主，四方修敬，皆遣上佐綱紀。

translations.literal: Huan Wen went down and garrisoned Gushu; awe and power shook the ruler; the four quarters in cultivating respect all sent senior aides and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen camped at Gushu, his might overshadowed the throne; every province sent chief secretaries to pay court.

sentences.zh: 彪之獨曰：「大司馬誠為富貴，朝廷既有宰相，動靜之宜自當諮稟。

translations.literal: Biao zhi alone said, “The grand marshal indeed is rich and noble; the court already has a chancellor—matters of movement and stillness naturally ought to be consulted and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Biao zhi said, “The grand marshal is already supreme, but the court still has a chancellor; major decisions belong in consultation with him.”

sentences.zh: 修敬若遣綱紀，致貢天子復何以過之！

translations.literal: If in cultivating respect one dispatches clerks, what could surpass presenting tribute to the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: If courtesy means dispatching secretaries, how is that different from paying homage only to the emperor?”

sentences.zh: 」竟不遣。

translations.literal: In the end he did not dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore sent no envoy to Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 溫以山陰縣折布米不時畢，郡不彈糾，上免彪之。

translations.literal: Wen because Shanyin County’s conversion of cloth to rice was not completed on time, and the commandery did not impeach, submitted and dismissed Biao zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen impeached Wang Biao zhi because Shanyin county delayed its cloth-for-rice levy and Kuaiji failed to discipline the magistrate.

sentences.zh: 彪之去郡，郡見罪謫未上州台者，皆原散之。

translations.literal: When Biao zhi left the commandery, those in the commandery seen guilty and demoted but not yet submitted to the provincial terrace, he all pardoned and released them.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving office he voided every local sentence that had not yet reached the provincial tribunal.

sentences.zh: 溫復以為罪，乃檻收下吏。

translations.literal: Wen again took it as a crime, then caged and seized him and handed him to subordinate clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen treated even that as an offense, threw him in a cage, and handed him to jailors.

sentences.zh: 會赦，免，左降謫為尚書。

translations.literal: It happened that there was an amnesty; he was pardoned, demoted on the left and relegated to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty freed him; he was reduced to ordinary minister of state.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復僕為射。

translations.literal: Before long, again he was vice director (she);
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again named vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是時溫將廢海西公，百僚震栗，溫亦色動，莫知所為。

translations.literal: At this time Wen was about to depose Duke Hai of the West; the hundred officials trembled; Wen also changed color and none knew what to do.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen prepared to depose Emperor Hai, the court froze; Huan Wen himself paled, unsure how to proceed.

sentences.zh: 彪之既知溫不臣跡已著，理不可奪。

translations.literal: Biao zhi already knew Wen’s unministerial traces were already manifest, principle could not be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi saw that Huan Wen’s usurpation was now plain and could not be denied.

sentences.zh: 乃謂溫曰：「公阿衡皇家，便當倚傍先代耳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he said to Wen, “You are pillar and balance to the imperial house; you ought to lean on earlier generations.
translations.idiomatic: He told Huan Wen, “You are the dynasty’s Huo Guang; look to the precedents of antiquity.”

sentences.zh: 」命取《霍光傳》。

translations.literal: He ordered fetch the “Huo Guang Traditions.”
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Archival “Life of Huo Guang” brought forward.

sentences.zh: 禮度儀制，定于須臾，曾無懼容。

translations.literal: Ritual demeanor and ceremonial regulation were settled in a moment; he had absolutely no fearful countenance.
translations.idiomatic: In minutes he laid out the ritual program, never flinching.

sentences.zh: 溫歎曰：「作元凱不當如是邪！

translations.literal: Wen sighed, saying, “Being Yuan and Kai ought not to be like this!”
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen marveled, “Even the ancient paragons Xi and Qi could not have done better!”

sentences.zh: 」時廢立之儀既絕於曠代，朝臣莫有識其故典者。

translations.literal: At that time the rites of deposition and enthronement had been cut off for remote generations; court ministers none knew their old precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Deposition protocol had been forgotten for generations; no minister remembered the forms.

sentences.zh: 彪之神彩毅然，朝服當階，文武儀准莫不取定，朝廷以此服之。

translations.literal: Biao zhi’s spirit bearing was firm; in court robes he blocked the steps; civil and military ceremony standards none did not take from his fixing; the court by this submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi, in full court dress on the palace steps, dictated every detail of the abdication ceremony, and the bureaucracy deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 溫又廢武陵王遵，以事示彪之。

translations.literal: Wen again deposed Prince Zun of Wuling and showed the affair to Biao zhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen next moved against Prince Sima Zun of Wuling, he consulted Wang Biao zhi.

sentences.zh: 彪之曰：「武陵親尊，未有顯罪，不可以猜嫌之間，便相廢徙。

translations.literal: Biao zhi said, “Wuling is kin and honored; he has no manifest crime; one cannot on the space of guess and suspicion then mutually demote and banish.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi objected: “The prince is close kin and highly placed; he has committed no clear crime—suspicion alone cannot justify his removal.”

sentences.zh: 公建立聖明，遐邇歸心，當崇獎王室，伊周同美。

translations.literal: You have established sagely clarity; far and near return hearts; you ought to exalt and reward the royal house, share in the beauty of Yi and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: You have enthroned a worthy sovereign and won the realm’s trust; you should exalt the house of Jin as Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou did.”

sentences.zh: 此大事，宜更深詳。

translations.literal: This is a great affair; ought to ponder it more deeply.
translations.idiomatic: This is too grave a matter to rush.”

sentences.zh: 」溫曰：「此已成事，卿勿復言。」

translations.literal: Wen said, “This is already accomplished; do not speak again.”
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen cut him off: “The matter is settled—say no more.”

sentences.zh: 及簡文崩，群臣疑惑，未敢立嗣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen died, the host of ministers was doubtful and did not dare establish an heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jianwen died, the court hesitated, afraid to name an heir.

sentences.zh: 或云，宜當須大司馬處分。

translations.literal: Some said one ought to await the grand marshal’s disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued the decision must wait on the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 彪之正色曰：「君崩，太子代立，大司馬何容得異！

translations.literal: Biao zhi in a stern voice said, “When the ruler dies, the crown prince replaces him—how can the grand marshal presume to differ!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi said flatly, “The heir succeeds when the sovereign dies—Huan Wen has no say in it.”

sentences.zh: 若先面諮，必反為所責矣。

translations.literal: If first one consults him to his face, one will surely in turn be blamed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Seek his nod first and you will only invite blame.”

sentences.zh: 」於是朝議乃定。

translations.literal: Thereupon court deliberation was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The court took his line and confirmed the succession.

sentences.zh: 及孝武帝即位，太皇太后令以帝沖幼，加在諒闇，令溫依周公居攝故事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, the grand empress dowager issued an order that because the emperor was young and still in the deep mourning hut, she ordered Wen to follow the Duke of Zhou’s regency precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu’s accession brought an edict from the grand empress dowager: the boy emperor was in mourning seclusion, so Huan Wen should act as regent after the Duke of Zhou model.

sentences.zh: 事已施行，彪之曰：「此異常大事，大司馬必當固讓，使萬機停滯，稽廢山陵，未敢奉令。

translations.literal: The affair had already been put in practice; Biao zhi said, “This is an extraordinary great affair; the grand marshal surely will firmly decline, causing the myriad tasks to halt and delaying the mausoleum works—I dare not accept the order.
translations.idiomatic: The rescript was about to issue when Wang Biao zhi protested, “Regency is too grave: Huan Wen will refuse, paralyze government, and delay the imperial tombs—I cannot endorse this.”

sentences.zh: 謹具封還內，請停。

translations.literal: I respectfully enclose and return it within; I request it be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the edict back to the palace and asked that it be withdrawn.”

sentences.zh: 」事遂不行。

translations.literal: The affair thereupon was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The plan died.

sentences.zh: 溫遇疾，諷朝廷求九錫，袁宏為文，以示彪之。

translations.literal: When Wen fell ill, he hinted to the court to request the Nine Bestowals; Yuan Hong composed the text and showed it to Biao zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ailing, Huan Wen hinted that the court award him the Nine Bestowals; Yuan Hong drafted the patent and showed it to Wang Biao zhi.

sentences.zh: 彪之視訖，歎其文辭之美，謂宏曰：「卿固大才，安可以此示人！

translations.literal: When Biao zhi finished viewing, he sighed at the beauty of its phrasing and said to Hong, “You are indeed a great talent—how can you show people this!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi read it through, praised Yuan Hong’s prose, then warned, “You are a great writer—never circulate a draft like this.”

sentences.zh: 」時謝安見其文，又頻使巨集改之，巨集遂逡巡其事。

translations.literal: At that time Xie An saw his text, and again repeatedly sent Ju Hong to revise it; Ju Hong thereupon hesitated over the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An also saw the draft and kept sending Yuan Hong back to revise it; Yuan Hong dragged his feet.

sentences.zh: 既屢引日，乃謀於彪之。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly drawn out days, then he consulted Biao zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Days stretched on until Yuan Hong sought Wang Biao zhi’s counsel.

sentences.zh: 彪之曰：「聞彼病日增，亦當不復支久，自可更小遲回。

translations.literal: Biao zhi said, “I hear that his illness daily increases; also he ought not again to endure long; naturally one can slightly delay and circle back.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi said, “Huan Wen worsens by the day; he cannot last—stall a little longer.”

sentences.zh: 」宏從之，溫亦尋薨。

translations.literal: Hong followed it; Wen also before long died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong obeyed; Huan Wen soon died.

sentences.zh: 時桓沖及安夾輔朝政，安以新喪元輔，主上未能親覽萬機，太皇太后宜臨朝，彪之曰：「先代前朝，主在繈抱，母子一體，故可臨朝。

translations.literal: At that time Huan Chong and Xie An jointly assisted court government; An because of the recent death of the chief pillar, the sovereign above was not yet able personally to oversee the myriad tasks, the grand empress ought to face the court; Biao zhi said, “In former generations of previous courts, when the ruler was in swaddling clothes, mother and child were one body, therefore she could face the court.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong and Xie An now co-ruled; Xie An argued that after losing the senior regent the young emperor could not manage every memorial, so the grand empress dowager should hold court. Wang Biao zhi answered, “Earlier dynasties allowed a regent mother only when the sovereign was still an infant in arms.”

sentences.zh: 太后亦不能決政事，終是顧問僕與君諸人耳。

translations.literal: The empress dowager also cannot decide administrative affairs; in the end it is only consulting ministers like you and me.
translations.idiomatic: Even then the dowager did not decide policy—she merely consulted ministers like us.”

sentences.zh: 今上年出十歲，垂婚冠，反令從嫂臨朝，示人君幼弱，豈是翼戴讚揚立德之謂乎！

translations.literal: Now the sovereign above is past ten years of age, nearing capping and marriage—on the contrary ordering a sister-in-law to face the court shows the ruler young and weak—how can this be what aiding and upholding and praising the establishment of virtue means!
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor is past ten, almost ready to marry and take the cap; having a sister-in-law preside would advertise his weakness—hardly how we “support the throne and build virtue.””

sentences.zh: 二君必行此事，豈僕所制，所惜者大體耳。

translations.literal: If the two lords must carry out this affair, how can it be within my servant’s control—the thing regretted is only the great frame.
translations.idiomatic: If you two insist, I cannot stop you—but think of the precedent you set.”

sentences.zh: 」時安不欲委任桓沖，故使太后臨朝決政，獻替專在乎自己。

translations.literal: At that time An did not wish to delegate authority to Huan Chong, therefore he had the empress dowager face the court and decide policy, so that submission and replacement lay solely with himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An really wanted to keep Huan Chong from power, so he used the dowager as a front while he pulled the strings.

sentences.zh: 彪之不達安旨，故以為言。

translations.literal: Biao zhi did not penetrate An’s intention; therefore he spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi did not grasp Xie An’s motive and argued as he did.

sentences.zh: 安竟不從。

translations.literal: An in the end did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An ignored him.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書令，與安共掌朝政。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred Minister of the Secretariat, sharing with An the grasp of court government.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Biao zhi became minister of the secretariat, sharing governance with Xie An.

sentences.zh: 安每曰：「朝之大事，衆不能決者，諮王公無不得判。

translations.literal: An often said, “Great affairs of court that the multitude cannot decide—whenever we consult the duke there is none he cannot judge.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An used to say, “Whenever the bureaucracy deadlocks, one audience with Duke Wang settles it.”

sentences.zh: 」以年老，上疏乞骸骨，詔不許。

translations.literal: Because of old age he submitted a memorial begging his bones; an edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Age drove him to ask retirement; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 轉拜護軍將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred General Who Guards the Army, with additional Cavalry-in-Attendance Without Specification.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to general who guards the army with the added title of cavalry attendant-at-large.

sentences.zh: 安欲更營宮室，彪之曰：「中興初，即位東府，殊為儉陋，元明二帝亦不改制。

translations.literal: An wished again to build palace halls; Biao zhi said, “At the beginning of the restoration, enthronement was at the Eastern Mansion—extremely frugal and mean; the two emperors Yuan and Ming also did not change the system.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An wanted new palace works; Wang Biao zhi objected that the court had begun in the cramped Eastern Mansion and that Emperors Yuan and Ming had never expanded it.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之亂，成帝止蘭台都坐，殆不蔽寒暑，是以更營修築。

translations.literal: In Su Jun’s turmoil, Emperor Cheng stopped at the Orchid Terrace common seat, barely sheltering from cold and heat; therefore they again built and repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun’s rebellion had forced Emperor Cheng into the Orchid Terrace offices, barely shielded from the elements—only then were modest repairs justified.

sentences.zh: 方之漢魏，誠為儉狹，復不至陋，殆合豐約之中，今自可隨宜增益修補而已。

translations.literal: Compared to Han and Wei, it is indeed cramped, yet again it does not reach meanness; it roughly fits between ample and restrained; now naturally one may follow suitability to increase and repair supplementarily.
translations.idiomatic: Beside Han and Wei palaces ours is small, yet not squalid—it strikes a balance; today we need only patch what is needed.

sentences.zh: 強寇未殄，正是休兵養士之時，何可大興功力，勞擾百姓邪！

translations.literal: The mighty foe is not yet exterminated; this is exactly the time to rest troops and nurture knights—how can one greatly raise works and toil and disturb the hundred surnames!
translations.idiomatic: Strong enemies remain; this is a time to rest armies and spare the people, not launch vast building projects.”

sentences.zh: 」安曰：「宮室不壯，後世謂人無能。

translations.literal: An said, “If palace halls are not grand, later generations will say people lack ability.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An answered, “If the halls are not magnificent, posterity will call us feeble.”

sentences.zh: 」彪之曰：」任天下事，當保國甯家，朝政惟允，豈以修屋宇為能邪！

translations.literal: Biao zhi said:” When bearing the realm’s tasks, one ought to protect the state and quiet the house; court government lies only in fairness—how can taking building palaces as ability be!”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi shot back, “Statesmen secure the altars and keep policy just—since when is masonry the test of ability!”

sentences.zh: 」安無以奪之。

translations.literal: An had nothing with which to refute him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An had no reply.

sentences.zh: 」故終彪之之世，不改營焉。

translations.literal: Therefore through Biao zhi’s lifetime they did not change construction.
translations.idiomatic: No palace overhaul occurred while Wang Biao zhi lived.

sentences.zh: 加光祿大夫、儀同三司，未拜。

translations.literal: He was given additional titles Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and ceremony equal to the Three Offices; he did not assume them.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered grand master of splendid happiness with three-ducal ceremony but never took up the seals.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，帝遣黃門侍郎問所苦，賜錢三十萬以營醫藥。

translations.literal: When his illness was grave, the emperor sent a Gentleman of the Yellow Gate to ask what pained him and granted three hundred thousand cash to supply medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When he worsened, the emperor sent a yellow-gate gentleman to inquire after his pain and three hundred thousand cash for physicians.

sentences.zh: 太元二年卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiyuan he died, age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Taiyuan, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 即以光祿為贈，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Grand Splendid Happiness as posthumous gift, posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as grand master of splendid happiness with the epithet Jian, “Concise.”

sentences.zh: 二子：越之，撫軍參軍；

translations.literal: Two sons: Yuezhi, adviser on the staff of the general who pacifies the army;
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Wang Yuezhi, aide to the pacification general, and

sentences.zh: 臨之，東陽太守。

translations.literal: Linzhi, Administrator of the Eastern Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Linzhi, prefect of Eastern Yang.

translations.literal: The chapter text records only an equals sign, a layout marker from the digitized source.

sentences.zh: 彬從兄棱

translations.literal: Bin’s older cousin Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling, elder cousin of Wang Bin

sentences.zh: =棱字文子，彬季父國子祭酒琛之子也。

translations.literal: = Ling’s courtesy name was Wenzi; he was the son of Bin’s youngest uncle, Libationer of the National Academy Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling, courtesy Wenzi, was a son of Wang Chen, the national-academy libationer—Wang Bin’s uncle by birth.

sentences.zh: 少曆清官。

translations.literal: In his youth he passed through pure offices.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career in unsullied posts.

sentences.zh: 渡江，為元帝丞相從事中郎。

translations.literal: Crossing the river, he became aide on the staff of Emperor Yuan’s chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yangzi he joined the chancellor’s staff under Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 從兄導以棱有政事，宜守大郡，乃出為豫章太守，加廣武將軍。

translations.literal: Older cousin Dao, because Ling had administrative ability, ought to guard a great commandery; thereupon he went out as Administrator of Yuzhang, with additional title General Who Extends Might.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao, seeing his talent for administration, sent him out as prefect of Yuzhang with the added rank of General Who Extends Might.

sentences.zh: 棱知從兄敦驕傲自負，有罔上心，日夕諫諍，以為宜自抑損，推崇盟主，且群從一門，並相與服事，應務相崇高，以隆勳業。

translations.literal: Ling knew his older cousin Dun was arrogant and self-satisfied and had a heart that disregarded the ruler; day and night he remonstrated bitterly, holding that Dun ought himself to restrain and diminish, exalt the covenant lord, and moreover the group of cousins in one gate all together serving ought in managing affairs mutually to exalt one another, in order to enlarge merit enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ling knew Wang Dun’s arrogance and disloyalty and remonstrated without rest: Dun must humble himself, honor the covenant chief, and let the whole Wang clan serve the throne in concert to enlarge their common achievement.

sentences.zh: 每言苦切。

translations.literal: Each time his words were bitterly cutting.
translations.idiomatic: His words were blunt to the point of pain.

sentences.zh: 敦不能容，潛使人害之。

translations.literal: Dun could not tolerate him and secretly sent men to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun could not bear the criticism and had him murdered in secret.

sentences.zh: 弟侃，亦知名，少曆顯職，位至吳國內史。

translations.literal: Younger brother Kan, also was renowned; in his youth he passed through illustrious posts, in rank reaching Internal Secretary of the Wu princedom.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Wang Kan also rose to fame, serving in high posts up to internal secretary of the Wu princedom.

sentences.zh: 虞潭

translations.literal: Yu Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan

sentences.zh: 虞潭，字思奧，會稽餘姚人，吳騎都尉翻之孫也。

translations.literal: Yu Tan, courtesy name Si’ao, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji, grandson of Wu Cavalry Commandant Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan, courtesy name Si’ao, came from Yuyao in Kuaiji and was a grandson of Yu Fan, Wu’s cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 父忠，仕至宜都太守。

translations.literal: His father Zhong reached in office Administrator of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu Zhong rose to prefect of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 吳之亡也，堅壁不降，遂死之。

translations.literal: When Wu perished, he held fast his walls and did not submit, thereupon died for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu fell he refused to surrender, held his walls, and died for his prince.

sentences.zh: 潭清貞有檢操，州辟從事、主簿，舉秀才，大司馬、齊王冏請為祭酒，除祁鄉令，徙醴陵令。

translations.literal: Tan was pure and chaste, with self-restraint; the province summoned him as clerk and chief secretary, he was raised as cultivated talent, the grand marshal Prince of Qi Jiong requested him as libationer, was appointed magistrate of Qixiang, transferred magistrate of Liling.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan was upright and disciplined: he served the province as clerk and chief clerk, passed the cultivated-talent exam, joined Prince Sima Jiong’s staff as libationer, then became magistrate of Qixiang and Liling.

sentences.zh: 值張昌作亂，郡縣多從之，潭獨起兵斬昌別率鄧穆等。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Chang rebelled; commanderies and counties mostly followed him; Tan alone raised troops and beheaded Chang’s detached leader Deng Mu and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chang rebelled and counties sided with him, Yu Tan alone raised a loyalist force and executed Zhang’s lieutenant Deng Mu.

sentences.zh: 襄陽太守華恢上潭領建平太守，以疾固辭。

translations.literal: Administrator of Xiangyang Hua Hui memorialized that Tan concurrently hold Administrator of Jianping; because of illness he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang prefect Hua Hui asked that Yu Tan also hold Jianping, but illness forced him to decline.

sentences.zh: 遂周旋征討，以軍功賜爵都亭侯。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went about on campaigns and punishments; by military merit he was granted fief as Marquis of the Metropolitan Village.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned through the rebellion and earned the duting marquisate.

sentences.zh: 陳敏反，潭東下討敏弟贊于江州。

translations.literal: Chen Min rebelled; Tan went east and punished Min’s younger brother Zan at Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Min revolted, Yu Tan marched east and crushed Chen Min’s brother Chen Zan in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史王矩上潭領廬陵太守。

translations.literal: Inspector of Guangzhou Wang Ju memorialized that Tan concurrently hold Administrator of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou inspector Wang Ju had him add the Luling prefecture.

sentences.zh: 綏撫荒餘，咸得其所。

translations.literal: He pacified and soothed the desolate remnants; all obtained their proper places.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the refugees and resettled every group.

sentences.zh: 又與諸軍共平陳恢，仍轉南康太守，進爵東鄉侯。

translations.literal: Again together with the various armies he jointly pacified Chen Hui, still was transferred Administrator of Nankang, advanced fief to Marquis of the Eastern Village.
translations.idiomatic: With the allied armies he next defeated Chen Hui, took Nankang, and was promoted to marquis of the eastern village.

sentences.zh: 尋被元帝檄，使討江州刺史華軼。

translations.literal: Before long he received Emperor Yuan’s dispatch ordering him to punish Inspector of Jiangzhou Hua Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan then ordered him against Jiangzhou inspector Hua Yi.

sentences.zh: 潭至廬陵，會軼已平，而湘川賊杜弢猶盛。

translations.literal: Tan reached Luling; it happened that Yi was already pacified, but the Xiang bandit Du Tao was still strong.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Luling, Hua Yi was already gone, but Du Tao still held the Xiang region.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史衛展上潭並領安成太守。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiangzhou Wei Zhan memorialized that Tan concurrently hold Administrator of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou inspector Wei Zhan added Ancheng to his portfolio.

sentences.zh: 時甘卓屯宜陽，為杜弢所逼。

translations.literal: At that time Gan Zhuo was encamped at Yiyang, pressed by Du Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo was trapped at Yiyang by Du Tao.

sentences.zh: 潭進軍救卓，卓上潭領長沙太守，固辭不就。

translations.literal: Tan advanced the army to rescue Zhuo; Zhuo memorialized that Tan concurrently hold Administrator of Changsha; he firmly declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan marched to relieve Gan Zhuo, who then asked the court to add Changsha—Yu Tan refused.

sentences.zh: 王敦版潭為湘東太守，復以疾辭。

translations.literal: Wang Dun by emergency commission made Tan Administrator of Xiangdong; again because of illness he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun’s field appointment made him Xiangdong prefect; again he pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 弢平後，元帝召補丞相軍諮祭酒，轉琅邪國中尉。

translations.literal: After Tao was pacified, Emperor Yuan summoned him to fill libationer-adviser on the chancellor’s staff, transferred interior commandant of the Langye princedom.
translations.idiomatic: After Du Tao fell, Emperor Yuan recalled him as army libationer-adviser, then made him interior commandant for the Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 帝為晉王，除屯騎校尉，徙右衛將軍，遷宗正卿，以疾告歸。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Jin, he was appointed Colonel of Garrison Cavalry, transferred Colonel of the Right Guard, promoted Director of the Imperial Clan, and because of illness requested return.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Rui was still prince of Jin, Yu Tan became colonel of garrison cavalry, then right guard, then director of the imperial clan; ill health sent him home.

sentences.zh: 會王含、沈充等攻逼京都，潭遂於本縣招合宗人，及郡中大姓，共起義軍，衆以萬數，自假明威將軍。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Han, Shen Chong, and others attacked and pressed the capital; Tan thereupon in his native county gathered clan members and the great surnames of the commandery, together raised a righteous army, the host numbering in the tens of thousands, and on his own authority took the title General Who Displays Bright Might.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Han and Shen Chong besieged the capital, Yu Tan rallied his lineage and the great clans of Yuyao, raised ten thousand loyalists, and styled himself General Who Displays Bright Might.

sentences.zh: 乃進赴國難，至上虞。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced to go to the state’s distress, reaching Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: He marched toward the capital as far as Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 明帝手詔潭為冠軍將軍，領會稽內史。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming by handwritten edict made Tan General Who Crowns the Army, concurrently Internal Secretary of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming’s autograph named him General Who Crowns the Army and internal secretary of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 潭即受命，義衆雲集。

translations.literal: Tan immediately received the command; righteous hosts gathered like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted at once, and loyalist bands flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 時有野鷹飛集屋梁，衆咸懼。

translations.literal: At that time there was a wild hawk that flew and perched on the roof beam; the host all feared.
translations.idiomatic: A wild hawk settled on his roofbeam and unnerved the troops.

sentences.zh: 潭曰：「起大義，而剛鷙之鳥來集，破賊必矣。

translations.literal: Tan said, “We raise great righteousness, and a fierce bird comes to perch—the bandits will surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan said, “We march in a just cause and a bird of prey alights on us—the rebels will break.”

sentences.zh: 」遣長史孔坦領前鋒過浙江，追躡充。

translations.literal: He dispatched chief clerk Kong Tan to lead the vanguard across the Zhe River, pursuing Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He sent chief clerk Kong Tan with the vanguard across the Zhe in pursuit of Shen Chong.

sentences.zh: 潭次於西陵，為坦後繼。

translations.literal: Tan halted at Xiling, as rear support for Kong Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan encamped at Xiling to back Kong Tan’s vanguard.

sentences.zh: 會充已擒，罷兵，徵拜尚書，尋補右衛將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: It happened that Chong was already captured; he dismissed troops, was summoned and appointed Minister, before long supplemented Colonel of the Right Guard, with additional Cavalry-in-Attendance Without Specification.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong was already taken; Yu Tan stood down his army, became a minister, soon added colonel of the right guard and cavalry attendant-at-large.

sentences.zh: 成帝即位，出為吳興太守，秩中二千石，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, he went out as Administrator of Wuxing, salary rank middle two thousand piculs, with additional title General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng he became prefect of Wuxing at two thousand piculs middle rank, with the added title General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 以討充功，進爵零縣侯。

translations.literal: By merit in punishing Chong, his fief was advanced to Marquis of Ling County.
translations.idiomatic: His part in defeating Shen Chong won him the marquisate of Ling county.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻反，加潭督三吳、晉陵、宣城、義興五郡軍事。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, Tan was given staff to supervise military affairs of the five commanderies Sanwu, Jinling, Xuancheng, and Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun’s revolt brought him command over the armies of Sanwu, Jinling, Xuancheng, and Yixing.

sentences.zh: 會王師敗績，大駕逼遷，潭勢弱，不能獨振，乃固守以俟四方之舉。

translations.literal: It happened that the royal army was defeated, the great chariot was forced to move; Tan’s strength was weak and he could not alone rouse himself; therefore he firmly guarded and awaited the four quarters’ rising.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops had collapsed and the court fled; too weak to strike alone, Yu Tan dug in and waited for allies.

sentences.zh: 會陶侃等下，潭與郗鑒、王舒協同義舉。

translations.literal: It happened that Tao Kan and others came down; Tan with Xi Jian and Wang Shu jointly coordinated the righteous undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Kan’s host arrived, Yu Tan coordinated with Xi Jian and Wang Shu.

sentences.zh: 侃等假潭節、監揚州浙江西軍事。

translations.literal: Kan and others lent Tan the tally and supervised military affairs west of the Zhe in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan gave him the credential axe and authority over Yangzhou west of the Zhe.

sentences.zh: 潭率衆與諸軍並勢，東西猗角。

translations.literal: Tan led the host together with the various armies in combined strength, east and west like ox-horns.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan joined the allied armies in a pincers east and west of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 遣督護沈伊距管商于吳縣，為商所敗，潭自貶還節。

translations.literal: He dispatched supervisor who protects Shen Yi to oppose Guan Shang at Wu county; Yi was defeated by Shang; Tan on his own demoted and returned the tally.
translations.idiomatic: His supervisor Shen Yi lost to Guan Shang at Wu; Yu Tan surrendered his staff of office in self-blame.

sentences.zh: 尋而峻平，潭以母老，輒去官還餘姚。

translations.literal: Before long Jun was pacified; Tan because his mother was old, then left office and returned to Yuyao to support her.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun fell he resigned to care for his aged mother in Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 詔轉鎮軍將軍、吳國內史。

translations.literal: An edict transferred him General Who Garrisons the Army, Internal Secretary of the Wu princedom.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled him as General Who Garrisons the Army and internal secretary of the Wu princedom.

sentences.zh: 復徙會稽內史，未發，還復吳郡。

translations.literal: Again he was moved Internal Secretary of Kuaiji; before he set out, he returned again to Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was slated for Kuaiji but returned to Wu instead.

sentences.zh: 以前後功，進爵武昌縣侯，邑一千六百戶。

translations.literal: By former and later merit, his fief was advanced to Marquis of Wuchang County, fief of one thousand six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Past and present service raised his fief to marquis of Wuchang with sixteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 是時軍荒之後，百姓饑饉，死亡塗地，潭乃表出倉米振救之。

translations.literal: At this time after the army’s famine, the hundred surnames were hungry and starved, death lay across the ground; Tan thereupon memorialized to release granary rice to relieve and save them.
translations.idiomatic: After the wartime famine corpses lined the roads; Yu Tan opened the granaries.

sentences.zh: 又修滬瀆壘，以防海抄，百轉賴之。

translations.literal: Again he repaired the Hudu's ramparts to guard against sea raiding; the hundred surnames relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the Hudu stockade against coastal raiders, to the people’s relief.

sentences.zh: 咸康中，進衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the middle of Xiankang, he was advanced General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Xiankang brought promotion to general who guards the army.

sentences.zh: 潭貌雖和弱，而內堅明，有膽決，雖屢統軍旅，而鮮有傾敗。

translations.literal: Although Tan’s appearance was mild and weak, within he was firm and bright, with courage and decision; although repeatedly he commanded armies and hosts, rarely was there overturn and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan looked mild but was steely within; despite many campaigns he seldom lost.

sentences.zh: 以毋憂去職。

translations.literal: Because of mourning for his mother he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for his mother forced him out.

sentences.zh: 服闕，以侍中、衛將軍徵。

translations.literal: When mourning clothes were ended, he was summoned as palace attendant and General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning the court summoned him as palace attendant and general who guards the army.

sentences.zh: 既至，更拜光祿大人、開府儀同三司，給親兵三百人，侍中如故。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was further appointed Grand Master of Splendid Radiance, opening office with ceremony equal to the Three Offices, given three hundred personal guards, palace attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he received grand master of splendid radiance, independent office with three-ducal ceremony, three hundred household guards, and kept his palace post.

sentences.zh: 年七十九，卒於位。

translations.literal: Age seventy-nine, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 追贈左光祿大夫，開府、侍中如故，諡曰孝烈。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Palace Attendant of the Left Grand Splendid Happiness, opening office and palace attendant as before; posthumous name Xiaolie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as palace attendant of the left and grand master of splendid happiness with his former titles restored; his epithet was Xiaolie, “Filial and Ardent.”

sentences.zh: 子仡嗣，官至右將軍司馬。

translations.literal: Son Yi inherited; in office he reached marshal of the general of the right.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu Yi succeeded him and rose to marshal of the right general.

sentences.zh: 仡卒，子嘯父嗣。

translations.literal: When Yi died, son Xiaofu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi’s son Yu Xiaofu inherited the title.

translations.literal: The chapter text records only an equals sign, a layout marker from the digitized source.

sentences.zh: 孫嘯父

translations.literal: Grandson Xiaofu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiaofu

sentences.zh: =嘯父少曆顯位，後至侍中，為孝武帝所親愛，嘗侍飲宴，帝從容問曰：「卿在門下，初不聞有所獻替邪？

translations.literal: = Xiaofu in his youth passed through illustrious posts, later reaching palace attendant, was intimately favored by Emperor Xiaowu; once attending a drinking feast, the emperor leisurely asked, “You are at the gate department—how is it I never hear you remonstrate or replace policy?”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiaofu rose through prominent posts to palace attendant, a favorite of Emperor Xiaowu. At a banquet the emperor teased him, “Since you joined my gate bureau, I have heard hardly a word of frank counsel from you.”

sentences.zh: 」嘯父家近海，謂帝有所求，對曰：「天時尚溫，{制魚}魚蝦鮓未可致，尋當有所上獻。

translations.literal: Xiaofu’s home was near the sea; thinking the emperor had a request, he answered, “The season is still warm; preserved fish and shrimp paste cannot yet be obtained; before long there ought to be something to present upward.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiaofu, whose home faced the sea, assumed the emperor wanted delicacies and answered, “The weather is still warm—salted fish and shrimp paste are not ready yet, but I will send some up soon.”

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly laughed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 因飲大醉，出，拜不能起，帝顧曰：「扶虞侍中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drank greatly drunk, went out, could not rise to bow; the emperor looked back, saying, “Support Attendant-in-chief Yu.”
translations.idiomatic: He drank himself insensible, staggered out, and could not bow; the emperor called, “Help Counselor Yu.”

sentences.zh: 」嘯父曰：「臣位未及扶，醉不及亂，非分之賜，所不敢當。

translations.literal: Xiaofu said, “My rank has not yet reached being supported; drunk I have not yet reached disorder; a favor beyond allotment—this your servant dares not accept.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiaofu replied, “I am not yet of the rank that needs an arm, nor drunk enough to need help—such favor is more than I may accept.”

sentences.zh: 」帝甚悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 隆安初，為吳國內史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Long’an, he was Internal Secretary of the Wu princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Long’an he became internal secretary of the Wu princedom.

sentences.zh: 征補尚書，未發，而王廞舉兵，版嘯父行吳興太守。

translations.literal: He was summoned to supplement Minister; before he set out, Wang Yin raised troops and by emergency commission made Xiaofu acting Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the ministry before Wang Yin rebelled and commissioned him acting prefect of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 嘯父即入吳興應廞。

translations.literal: Xiaofu immediately entered Wuxing to respond to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiaofu marched into Wuxing to support Wang Yin.

sentences.zh: 廞敗，有司奏嘯父與廞同謀，罪應斬。

translations.literal: When Yin was defeated, the responsible officials memorialized that Xiaofu had plotted together with Yin; by guilt he ought to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Yin’s defeat the ministry charged Yu Xiaofu as co-conspirator, a capital crime.

sentences.zh: 詔以祖潭舊勳，聽以疾贖為庶人。

translations.literal: An edict because of grandfather Tan’s old merit permitted him by illness to ransom himself as commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The throne, remembering Yu Tan’s service, allowed him to commute sentence to commoner status for reasons of health.

sentences.zh: 四年，復拜尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, again he was appointed Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he was again named minister.

sentences.zh: 桓玄用事，以為太尉左司馬。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan wielded power, he was made senior aide to the left of the grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huan Xuan he became senior aide on the left of the grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 尋遷護軍將軍，出為會稽內史。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred General Who Guards the Army, went out as Internal Secretary of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was general who guards the army and internal secretary of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，去職，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi, he left office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yixi he retired and died at home.

translations.literal: The chapter text records only an equals sign, a layout marker from the digitized source.

sentences.zh: 兄子𩦎

translations.literal: Older brother’s son Mo (written 𩦎).
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan’s nephew Yu Mo (the received text writes his personal name with the rare character 𩦎).

sentences.zh: =𩦎字思行，潭之兄子也。

translations.literal: = Mo’s courtesy name was Sixing; he was Tan’s older brother’s son.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Mo, courtesy Sixing, was the son of Yu Tan’s elder brother.

sentences.zh: 雖機幹不及於潭，然而素行過之。

translations.literal: Although planning ability did not match Tan, yet in plain conduct he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: He lacked Yu Tan’s political flair but surpassed him in personal integrity.

sentences.zh: 與譙國桓彝俱為吏部郎，情好甚篤。

translations.literal: Together with Huan Yi of Qiao commandery he both was Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel; their affection was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: He and Huan Yi of Qiao both served as gentlemen of the ministry of personnel and became close friends.

sentences.zh: 彝遣溫拜𩦎，𩦎使子穀拜彝。

translations.literal: Yi sent Wen to bow to Mo; Mo sent his son Gu to bow to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi had Huan Wen pay a formal call on Yu Mo; Yu Mo had his son Yu Gu return the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 曆吳興太守、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He passed through Administrator of Wuxing, golden purple Grand Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Wuxing and golden-purple grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 王導嘗謂𩦎曰：「孔愉有公才而無公望，丁潭有公望而無公才，兼之者，其在卿乎！

translations.literal: Wang Dao once said to Mo, “Kong Yu has ducal talent but lacks ducal stature; Ding Tan has ducal stature but lacks ducal talent—he who combines them—is it perhaps in you!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao once told him, “Kong Yu has the makings of a statesman but not the presence; Ding Tan has the presence but not the substance—perhaps you unite both.”

sentences.zh: 」官未達而喪，時人惜之。

translations.literal: Before office was reached he died; people of the time regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: He died before reaching high office, to contemporaries’ regret.

sentences.zh: 子谷，位至吳國內史。

translations.literal: Son Gu, in rank reached Internal Secretary of the Wu princedom.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu Gu rose to internal secretary of the Wu princedom.

sentences.zh: 顧衆

translations.literal: Gu Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong

sentences.zh: 顧衆，字長始，吳郡吳人，驃騎將軍榮之族弟也。

translations.literal: Gu Zhong, courtesy name Changshi, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery, a clansman younger brother of General of Agile Cavalry Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong, courtesy Changshi, was a native of Wu county and a kinsman of Gu Rong, general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父秘，交州刺史，有文武才幹。

translations.literal: His father Mi was Inspector of Jiaozhou and had civil and martial talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gu Mi had been inspector of Jiaozhou, a man of both civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 衆出後伯父，早終，事伯母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Zhong went out as heir to his uncle by father, who died early; he served his aunt by marriage and was heard of for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong was adopted to his late uncle’s line and earned a reputation for filial care of his aunt.

sentences.zh: 光祿硃誕器之。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Zhu Dan esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Dan, grand master of splendid happiness, singled him out for praise.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿，舉秀才，除余杭、秣陵令，並不行。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as chief secretary, raised him as cultivated talent, appointed magistrate of Yuhang and Moling—both he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The province named him chief clerk and recommended him as cultivated talent; appointments to Yuhang and Moling he declined.

sentences.zh: 元帝為鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan was General Who Garrisons the East.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan held the eastern headquarters,

sentences.zh: 命為參軍。

translations.literal: he ordered him to be aide on the staff.
translations.idiomatic: he named Gu Zhong a staff aide.

sentences.zh: 以討華軼功，封東鄉侯，辟丞相掾。

translations.literal: By merit in punishing Hua Yi he was enfeoffed Marquis of the Eastern Village, summoned as retainer of the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He earned the eastern-village marquisate against Hua Yi and joined the chancellor’s secretariat.

sentences.zh: 秘卒，州人立衆兄壽為刺史，為州人所害，衆往交州迎喪，值杜弢之亂，崎嶇六年乃還。

translations.literal: When Mi died, the people of the province set up Zhong’s older brother Shou as inspector; he was killed by the people of the province; Zhong went to Jiaozhou to welcome the coffin; it happened that there was Du Tao’s turmoil; rugged six years then he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu Mi died the locals tried to make Gu Zhong’s brother Gu Shou inspector; rioters murdered Gu Shou; Gu Zhong went south to fetch his father’s bier, was trapped six years by Du Tao’s rebellion, and only then got home.

sentences.zh: 秘曾蒞吳興，吳興義故以衆經離寇難，共遺錢二百萬，一無所受。

translations.literal: Mi once had attended Wu Xing; Wu Xing righteous associates because Zhong had passed through bandit hardship together presented cash two hundred thousand—he accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Mi had once governed Wuxing; old friends there, pitying Gu Zhong’s ordeal under the rebels, offered two million cash, which he refused.

sentences.zh: 及帝踐阼，徵拜駙馬都尉、奉朝請，轉尚書郎。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he was summoned and appointed Commandant of the Household for the Heir-apparent and court attendant, transferred Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Yuan’s accession he became commandant for the heir-apparent and court attendant, then gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 大將軍王敦請為從事中郎，上補南康太守。

translations.literal: Grand General Wang Dun requested him as aide on the staff; he was submitted to supplement Administrator of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun recruited him as staff aide and nominated him for Nankang.

sentences.zh: 會詔除鄱陽太守，加廣武將軍。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict appointed Administrator of Poyang, with additional title General Who Extends Might.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up Nankang, an edict named him prefect of Poyang with the added rank of General Who Extends Might.

sentences.zh: 衆徑之鄱陽，不過敦，敦甚怪焉。

translations.literal: Zhong went straight to Poyang and did not call on Dun; Dun greatly wondered at it.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong went straight to Poyang without visiting Wang Dun, who took deep offense.

sentences.zh: 及敦構逆，令衆出軍，衆遲回不發。

translations.literal: When Dun plotted rebellion, he ordered Zhong to dispatch troops; Zhong delayed and did not issue.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rebelled he ordered Gu Zhong to mobilize; Gu Zhong stalled.

sentences.zh: 敦大怒，以軍期召衆還，詰之，聲色甚厲。

translations.literal: Dun was greatly angry; with military deadline he summoned Zhong back, questioned him, voice and color very severe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun recalled him under military deadline and berated him furiously.

sentences.zh: 衆不為動容，敦意漸釋。

translations.literal: Zhong did not change countenance; Dun’s intention gradually released.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong never flinched; Wang Dun’s rage slowly cooled.

sentences.zh: 時敦又怒宣城內史陸喈，衆又辨明之。

translations.literal: At that time Dun again was angry at Internal Secretary of Xuancheng Lu Kai; Zhong again cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun next turned on Xuancheng prefect Lu Kai, Gu Zhong cleared him again.

sentences.zh: 敦長史陸玩在坐，代衆危懼，出謂衆曰：「卿真所謂剛亦不吐，柔亦不茹，雖仲山甫何以加之！

translations.literal: Dun’s chief clerk Lu Wan was seated there; for Zhong he was fearful in his place; going out he said to Zhong, “You truly are what is called ‘hard he does not spit out, soft he does not chew down’—even Zhong Shanfu—how could one add to that!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun’s chief clerk Lu Wan, terrified for Gu Zhong, told him afterward, “You are ‘hard or soft, nothing swallowed wrong’—even Zhong Shanfu could do no more.”

sentences.zh: 」敦事捷，欲以衆為吳興內史。

translations.literal: When Dun’s affair succeeded, he wished to make Zhong Internal Secretary of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun’s coup he wanted Gu Zhong as prefect of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 衆固辭，舉吏部郎桓彝，彝亦讓衆，事並不行。

translations.literal: Zhong firmly declined, recommending Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel Huan Yi; Yi also yielded to Zhong; the affair altogether was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong refused and nominated Huan Yi; Huan Yi yielded back; nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 敦鎮姑孰，復以衆為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Dun garrisoned Gushu, again he made Zhong aide on the staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun moved to Gushu he again put Gu Zhong on his staff.

sentences.zh: 敦平，除太子中庶子，為義興太守，加揚威將軍。

translations.literal: When Dun was pacified, he was appointed junior mentor to the heir, was Administrator of Yixing, with additional title General Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion he became junior mentor to the crown prince, prefect of Yixing, and General Who Displays Might.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻反，王師敗績，衆還吳，潛圖義舉。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, the royal army was defeated; Zhong returned to Wu and secretly plotted a righteous undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun crushed the imperial army, Gu Zhong slipped back to Wu to organize resistance.

sentences.zh: 時吳國內史庾冰奔於會稽，峻以蔡謨代之。

translations.literal: At that time Internal Secretary of the Wu princedom Yu Bing fled to Kuaiji; Jun made Cai Mo replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu princedom internal secretary Yu Bing fled to Kuaiji; Su Jun installed Cai Mo.

sentences.zh: 前陵江將軍張悊為峻收兵于吳，衆遣人喻悊，悊從之。

translations.literal: Former General Who Clears the River Zhang Zhi for Jun gathered troops at Wu; Zhong sent men to instruct Zhi; Zhi followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Former river-clearing general Zhang Zhi was raising troops for Su Jun; Gu Zhong won him over.

sentences.zh: 衆乃遣郎中徐機告謨曰：「衆已潛闔家兵，待時而奮，又與張悊克期效節。

translations.literal: Zhong thereupon dispatched Gentleman Xu Ji to tell Mo, “Zhong has already secretly closed household troops, awaiting the time to rouse; again with Zhang Zhi has fixed a date to devote loyalty.”
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong sent Xu Ji to tell Cai Mo that he had armed his household and allied with Zhang Zhi for a coordinated strike.

sentences.zh: 」謨乃檄衆為本國督護，揚威將軍仍舊，衆從弟護軍將軍颺為威遠將軍、前鋒督護。

translations.literal: Mo thereupon issued a dispatch making Zhong supervisor who protects his native commandery, General Who Displays Might as before; Zhong’s younger cousin by the father General Who Guards the Army Yang was General Who Displays Far Might, vanguard supervisor who protects.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo then commissioned Gu Zhong as native-place supervisor with his old brevet rank, while Gu Zhong’s cousin Gu Yang became General Who Displays Far Might and vanguard coordinator.

sentences.zh: 吳中人士同時響應。

translations.literal: Notables of Wu at the same time responded.
translations.idiomatic: Wu gentry rose with them.

sentences.zh: 峻遣將弘徽領甲卒五百，鼓行而前。

translations.literal: Jun dispatched general Hong Hui to lead five hundred armored soldiers, drumming and advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun sent Hong Hui with five hundred armored men marching to the drum.

sentences.zh: 衆與颺、悊要擊徽，戰于高莋，大破之，收其軍實。

translations.literal: Zhong with Yang and Zhi intercepted Hui, battled at Gao zuo, greatly defeated him, and collected his military stores.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong, Gu Yang, and Zhang Zhi ambushed Hong Hui at Gao zuo, routed him, and seized his supplies.

sentences.zh: 謨以冰當還任，故便去郡。

translations.literal: Mo because Bing ought to return to office, therefore then left the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo expected Yu Bing back and vacated the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 衆遣颺率諸軍屯無錫。

translations.literal: Zhong dispatched Yang to lead the various armies and encamp at Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong sent Gu Yang to encamp at Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 冰至，鎮禦亭，恐賊從海虞道入，衆自往備之。

translations.literal: When Bing arrived, he garrisoned Yuting, fearing the bandits would enter by the Haiyu road; Zhong himself went to prepare it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing held Yuting while Gu Zhong covered the Haiyu approach.

sentences.zh: 而賊率張健、馬流攻無錫，颺等大敗，庚冰亦失守，健等遂據吳城。

translations.literal: But the bandit leaders Zhang Jian and Ma Liu attacked Wuxi; Yang and the others were greatly defeated; Yu Bing also lost his defense; Jian and the others thereupon occupied Wu city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian and Ma Liu struck Wuxi, shattered Gu Yang, and Yu Bing lost Yuting as well; the rebels seized Wu.

sentences.zh: 衆自海虞由婁縣東倉與賊別率交戰，破之，義軍又集進屯烏苞。

translations.literal: Zhong from Haiyu by Lou county east granary joined battle with a detached band of bandits, defeated them, and the righteous army again gathered advance and encamped at Wubao.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong slipped from Haiyu through Lou county, beat a rebel detachment at the east granary, and rallied loyalists at Wubao.

sentences.zh: 會稽內史王舒、吳興內史虞潭並檄衆為五郡大督護，統諸義軍討健。

translations.literal: Internal Secretary of Kuaiji Wang Shu and Internal Secretary of Wuxing Yu Tan jointly dispatched Zhong as supervisor who protects the five commanderies, commanding the various righteous armies to punish Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu of Kuaiji and Yu Tan of Wuxing named Gu Zhong coordinator of five commanderies to attack Zhang Jian.

sentences.zh: 潭遣將姚休為衆前鋒，與賊戰沒。

translations.literal: Tan dispatched general Yao Xiu as Zhong’s vanguard and battled with the bandits; he perished.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan’s vanguard Yao Xiu died fighting the rebels.

sentences.zh: 衆還守紫壁。

translations.literal: Zhong returned and guarded Zibi.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong fell back to Zibi.

sentences.zh: 時賊党方銳，義軍沮退，人咸勸衆過浙江。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit faction was just sharp; the righteous army was dispirited and retreated; people all urged Zhong to cross the Zhe River.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel morale was high and loyalists wavered; many urged Gu Zhong to withdraw south of the Zhe.

sentences.zh: 衆曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Zhong said, “It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong said, “No.”

sentences.zh: 今保固紫壁，可得全錢唐以南五縣。

translations.literal: Now if we protect and firm Zibi, we can preserve the five counties south of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: If we hold Zibi we keep the five counties south of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 若越他境，便為寓軍，控引無所，非長計也。

translations.literal: If we cross into other territory, then we become a guest army with nowhere to draw support—not a long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: If we flee south we become homeless auxiliaries with no base—that is no strategy.”

sentences.zh: 」臨平人範明亦謂衆曰：「此地險要，可以制寇，不可委也。

translations.literal: A man of Linping, Fan Ming, also said to Zhong, “This terrain is strategically vital; it can control bandits—it cannot be abandoned.”
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ming of Linping added, “This ground is the key to the defense—we dare not yield it.”

sentences.zh: 」衆乃版明為參軍。

translations.literal: Zhong thereupon by emergency commission made Ming aide on the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong breveted Fan Ming as staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 明率宗黨五百人，合諸軍，凡四千人，復進討健。

translations.literal: Ming led lineage party five hundred men, combined with the various armies, in all four thousand men, again advanced to punish Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ming led five hundred kinsmen; with allies they mustered four thousand and struck Zhang Jian again.

sentences.zh: 健退于曲阿，留錢弘為吳令。

translations.literal: Jian retreated to Qu’a, left Qian Hong as magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian fell back to Qu’a and left Qian Hong as Wu magistrate.

sentences.zh: 軍次路丘，即斬弘首。

translations.literal: The army halted at Luqiu; immediately they beheaded Hong’s head.
translations.idiomatic: The loyalists camped at Luqiu and beheaded Qian Hong.

sentences.zh: 衆進住吳城，遣督護硃祈等九軍，與蘭陵太守李閎共守庱亭。

translations.literal: Zhong advanced and stopped at Wu city, dispatched supervisor who protects Zhu Qi and nine armies together with Administrator of Lanling Li Min to jointly guard Kuangting.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong reoccupied Wu, sent Zhu Qi with nine columns alongside Lanling prefect Li Min to hold Kuangting.

sentences.zh: 健遣馬流、陶陽等往攻之。

translations.literal: Jian dispatched Ma Liu, Tao Yang, and others to go attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian sent Ma Liu and Tao Yang against them.

sentences.zh: 閎與祈等逆擊，大破之，斬首二千餘級。

translations.literal: Min with Qi and the others struck them head-on, greatly defeated them, beheading more than two thousand grades.
translations.idiomatic: Li Min and Zhu Qi counterattacked, killing over two thousand.

sentences.zh: 峻平，論功，衆以承檄備義，推功於謨，謨以衆唱謀，非己之力，俱表相讓，論者美之。

translations.literal: When Jun was pacified, judging merit, Zhong because he had received the dispatch and prepared righteousness, pushed merit to Mo; Mo because Zhong had initiated the plan, it was not his own strength; both memorialized yielding to each other; discussers praised them.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun fell, Gu Zhong credited Cai Mo for the coalition order while Cai Mo credited Gu Zhong’s initiative; their mutual deference drew praise.

sentences.zh: 封鄱陽縣伯，除平南軍司，不就。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Marquis of Poyang County, appointed director of staff for the army of the General Who Pacifies the South; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was ennobled as marquis of Poyang and named army director under the General Who Pacifies the South but declined.

sentences.zh: 更拜丹陽尹、本國大中正，入為侍中，轉尚書。

translations.literal: Again he was appointed chief of Danyang, grand rectifier of his native commandery, entered as palace attendant, transferred Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief of Danyang, native-place grand rectifier, palace attendant, then minister.

sentences.zh: 咸康末，遷領軍將軍、揚州大中正，固讓不拜。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiankang, he was transferred General Who Leads the Army and grand rectifier of Yangzhou; firmly he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xiankang he was offered general who leads the army and Yangzhou grand rectifier; he refused.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Because of mourning for his mother he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for his mother forced him out.

sentences.zh: 穆帝即位，何充執政，復征衆為領軍，不起。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mu ascended the throne, He Chong held power; again he summoned Zhong as General Who Leads the Army; he did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mu, He Chong recalled him as general who leads the army; he stayed home.

sentences.zh: 服闕，乃就。

translations.literal: When mourning clothes were ended, then he went to it.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning term ended he accepted.

sentences.zh: 是時充與武陵王不平，衆會通其間，遂得和釋。

translations.literal: At this time Chong and the Prince of Wuling were not at peace; Zhong met and communicated between them; thereupon they obtained harmony and release.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong feuded with the Prince of Wuling; Gu Zhong mediated until peace returned.

sentences.zh: 充崇信佛教，衆議其糜費，每以為言。

translations.literal: Chong venerated and believed Buddhism; Zhong discussed its waste; each time he spoke on it.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong lavishly patronized Buddhism; Gu Zhong criticized the expense whenever he could.

sentences.zh: 嘗與充同載，經佛寺，充要衆入門。

translations.literal: Once he rode together with Chong, passed a Buddhist monastery; Chong invited Zhong to enter the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Once, riding with He Chong past a monastery, He Chong asked him inside.

sentences.zh: 衆不下車。

translations.literal: Zhong did not descend from the cart.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong stayed in the carriage.

sentences.zh: 充以衆州裏宿望，每優遇之。

translations.literal: Chong because Zhong was a senior figure of the province and village, each time treated him preferentially.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong still honored him as an elder of their home commandery.

sentences.zh: 以年老，上疏乞骸骨，詔書不許。

translations.literal: Because of old age he submitted a memorial begging his bones; the edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he asked to retire; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書僕射。

translations.literal: He was transferred Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 永和二年卒，時年七十三。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghe he died, at the time age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yonghe, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 追贈特進、光祿大夫，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded specially advanced, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously advanced to specially advanced and grand master of splendid happiness with the epithet Jing, “Tranquil.”

sentences.zh: 長子昌嗣，為建康令。

translations.literal: The eldest son Chang inherited; he was magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Gu Chang succeeded him and served as magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 第三子會，中軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: The third son Hui, adviser on the staff of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Gu Hui was an aide on the central army staff.

sentences.zh: 時稱美士。

translations.literal: At the time he was called a fine gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries ranked him among the finest gentlemen of the age.

sentences.zh: 張闓

translations.literal: Zhang Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai

sentences.zh: 張闓，字敬緒，丹陽人，吳輔吳將軍昭之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Zhang Kai, courtesy name Jingxu, was a man of Danyang, great-grandson of Wu’s auxiliary general Zhang Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai, courtesy Jingxu, came from Danyang and was a great-grandson of Zhang Zhao, who had served Wu as auxiliary general.

sentences.zh: 少孤，有志操。

translations.literal: In his youth he was orphaned; he had aspiration and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he showed both ambition and integrity.

sentences.zh: 太常薛兼進之於元帝，言闓才幹貞固，當今之良器。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Xue Jian advanced him to Emperor Yuan, saying Kai’s talent and capacity were chaste and firm—today’s fine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master Xue Jian recommended him to Emperor Yuan as a man of steadfast talent—the sort of vessel the age needed.

sentences.zh: 即引為安東參軍，甚加禮遇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was led in as aide on the staff of General Who Pacifies the East; he was greatly shown ritual favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan named him aide on the eastern headquarters staff and treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 轉丞相從事中郎，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He was transferred aide on the chancellor’s staff; because of mourning for his mother he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the chancellor’s staff, then resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 既葬，帝強起之，闓固辭疾篤。

translations.literal: After burial, the emperor strongly ordered him to rise; Kai firmly declined, claiming grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral the emperor ordered him back to duty; Zhang Kai pleaded grave illness.

sentences.zh: 優命敦逼，遂起視事。

translations.literal: Favoring edicts pressed urgently; thereupon he rose and attended to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated rescripts pressed him until he returned to his desk.

sentences.zh: 及帝為晉王，拜給事黃門侍郎，領本郡大中正。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Jin, he was appointed Gentleman for Court Affairs at the Yellow Gate, concurrently grand rectifier of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Rui was still prince of Jin, Zhang Kai became gentleman for court affairs at the yellow gate and native-place grand rectifier.

sentences.zh: 以佐翼勳，賜爵丹陽縣侯，遷侍中。

translations.literal: By merit in assisting the wings, he was granted fief as Marquis of Danyang County, transferred palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: For aiding the prince’s rise he received the Danyang marquisate and a palace post.

sentences.zh: 帝踐阼，出補晉陵內史，在郡甚有威惠。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he went out to supplement Internal Secretary of Jinling; in the commandery he had very much awe and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: At the accession he became internal secretary of Jinling, ruling with both authority and kindness.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔曰：「夫二千石之任，當勉勵其德，綏齊所蒞，使寬而不縱，嚴而不苛，其于勤功督察，便國利人，抑強扶弱，使無雜濫，真太守之任也。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict, saying, “The charge of the two-thousand-picul rank ought to encourage their virtue, pacify and order what they attend, so that there is leniency without laxity, severity without harshness; as to diligent merit and supervision, benefiting the state and profiting the people, suppressing the strong and supporting the weak, so that there is no mixing and overflow—this is truly the charge of a grand administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor published an edict praising the true prefect’s task: lenient yet not lax, strict yet not cruel, aiding the weak and checking the strong.

sentences.zh: 若聲過其實，古人所不取。

translations.literal: If reputation surpasses the reality, the ancients did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Reputation without substance the sages rejected.

sentences.zh: 功乎異端，為政之甚害，蓋所貴者本也。

translations.literal: Merit in strange byways is a great harm to governing; what is prized is the root.
translations.idiomatic: Novelty-seeking harms government; the root is what matters.”

sentences.zh: 」闓遵而行之。

translations.literal: Kai obeyed and practiced it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai took the admonition as his standard.

sentences.zh: 時所部四縣並以旱失田，闓乃立曲阿新豐塘，溉田八百餘頃，每歲豐稔。

translations.literal: At that time the four counties under his jurisdiction all because of drought lost fields; Kai thereupon built the Qu’a Xinfeng pond, irrigating more than eight hundred qing of fields; each year there was abundant harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Drought had ruined the four counties under him, so he built the Xinfeng reservoir at Qu’a, irrigating over eight hundred qing of good land and securing yearly harvests.

sentences.zh: 葛洪為其頌。

translations.literal: Ge Hong composed a eulogy for him.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong wrote a hymn to the project.

sentences.zh: 計用二十一萬一千四百二十功，以擅興造免官。

translations.literal: The reckoning used two hundred eleven thousand four hundred twenty work-units; because he presumptuously raised construction he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The works consumed 211,420 labor units; unauthorized building cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 後公卿並為之言曰：「張闓興陂溉田，可謂益國，而反被黜，使臣下難復為善。

translations.literal: Later dukes and ministers together spoke for him, saying, “Zhang Kai raised dikes and irrigated fields—this can be called benefiting the state—yet on the contrary he was dismissed, making it hard for ministers below again to do good.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials petitioned: “Zhang Kai’s waterworks helped the empire—punishing him discourages every good deed.”

sentences.zh: 」帝感悟，乃下詔曰：「丹陽侯闓昔以勞役部人免官，雖從吏議，猶未掩其忠節之志也。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and thereupon issued an edict, saying, “Marquis of Danyang Kai formerly because of corvée laboring his people was removed from office; although following clerical deliberation, still it did not cover his intent of loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented: “Though the ministry cashiered Marquis Zhang for overworking the people, his loyal intent should not be buried.”

sentences.zh: 倉廩國之大本，宜得其才，今以闓為大司農。

translations.literal: Granaries are the state’s great root; one ought to obtain the right talent for them; now appoint Kai as Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries are the state’s foundation—name Zhang Kai minister of agriculture.”

sentences.zh: 」闓陳黜免始爾，不宜便居九列。

translations.literal: Kai stated that dismissal had just begun; it was not fitting immediately to occupy the nine ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai protested that a man just stripped of office should not vault into the nine senior ministries.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，不許，然後就職。

translations.literal: He submitted the memorial; it was not permitted; then he assumed office.
translations.idiomatic: The throne refused his memorial, and he took up the seal.

sentences.zh: 帝晏駕，以闓為大匠卿，營建平陵，事畢，遷尚書。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Kai was made grand master builder to construct Jianping Mausoleum; when the task was finished, he was transferred Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He directed Emperor Yuan’s tomb works, then became a minister of state.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之役，闓與王導俱入宮侍衛。

translations.literal: In Su Jun’s campaign, Kai together with Wang Dao both entered the palace to attend and guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Jun’s revolt he entered the palace with Wang Dao to defend the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 峻使闓持節權督東軍。

translations.literal: Jun ordered Kai to hold the tally and act as supervisor of the eastern armies.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun made him credential-bearing supervisor of eastern forces.

sentences.zh: 王導潛與闓謀，密宣太后詔于三吳，令速起義軍。

translations.literal: Wang Dao secretly plotted with Kai, secretly proclaiming the empress dowager’s edict in Sanwu, ordering them quickly to raise righteous armies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao conspired with him to circulate the empress dowager’s call for loyalist armies in the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 陶侃等至，假闓節，行征虜將軍，與振威將軍陶回共督丹陽義軍。

translations.literal: When Tao Kan and others arrived, they lent Kai the tally, acting as General Who Captures Caitiffs, together with General Who Displays Might Tao Hui jointly supervising Danyang righteous armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Kan arrived, Zhang Kai received brevet rank as General Who Captures Caitiffs and, with Tao Hui, commanded the Danyang loyalists.

sentences.zh: 闓到晉陵，使內史劉耽盡以一部穀，並遣吳郡度支運四部穀，以給車騎將軍郗鑒。

translations.literal: Kai reached Jinling, ordered Internal Secretary Liu Dan to give all the grain of one command, and also dispatched Wu commandery transport to move four commanderies’ grain to supply General of Chariots and Cavalry Xi Jian.
