translations.idiomatic: At Jinling he had Liu Dan release one full granary and routed four convoys of grain from Wu to feed Xi Jian’s army.

sentences.zh: 又與吳郡內史蔡謨、前吳興內史虞潭、會稽內史王舒等招集義兵，以討峻。

translations.literal: Again together with Internal Secretary of Wu Cai Mo, former Internal Secretary of Wuxing Yu Tan, Internal Secretary of Kuaiji Wang Shu, and others he recruited righteous troops to punish Jun.
translations.idiomatic: With Cai Mo, Yu Tan, Wang Shu, and others he raised militias against Su Jun.

sentences.zh: 峻平，以尚書加散騎常侍，賜爵宜陽伯。

translations.literal: When Jun was pacified, by Minister with additional Cavalry-in-Attendance Without Specification he was granted fief as Baron of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory he kept his ministerial post, added cavalry attendant-at-large, and received the Yiyang barony.

sentences.zh: 遷廷尉，以疾解職，拜金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred Minister of Justice; because of illness he resigned office, was appointed golden purple Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him from the ministry of justice; he retired as golden-purple grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: Before long he died, at the time age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 子混嗣。

translations.literal: Son Hun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Hun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 闓箋表文議傳於世。

translations.literal: Kai’s memorials, petitions, essays, and deliberations were handed down in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials and state papers circulated for generations.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historian’s appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: Historian’s appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：季孫行父稱見有禮於其君者，如孝子之養父母；

translations.literal: The historian says: Ji Sun Xingfu declared that seeing one who has ritual toward his ruler is like a filial son nurturing parents;
translations.idiomatic: The historians wrote: Ji Sun Xingfu said that ministers who honor their ruler resemble dutiful children,

sentences.zh: 無禮於其君者，如鷹鸇之逐鳥雀。

translations.literal: seeing one who lacks ritual toward his ruler is like a hawk or kite chasing birds and sparrows.
translations.idiomatic: while those who insult him are hawks tearing at sparrows.

sentences.zh: 是以石碏戮厚，叔向誅鮒，前史以為美譚。

translations.literal: Therefore Shi Que executed Hou, Shu Xiang executed Fu; former histories took them as fine tales.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Shi Que executed his son and Shu Xiang his nephew—old histories praised such rectitude.

sentences.zh: 王敦之惡，不足矜其類。

translations.literal: Wang Dun’s wickedness is not enough to pity his kind.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun’s infamy hardly earns sympathy for his whole clan.

sentences.zh: 然而硃家容布，為大俠之首；

translations.literal: Yet Zhu Jia harbored Ji Bu and was chief among great knights-errant;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jia’s sheltering of Ji Bu made him the model knight-errant,

sentences.zh: 酈寄載呂，興賣友之譏。

translations.literal: Ying Ji carried Lü Lu and aroused the ridicule of selling friends.
translations.idiomatic: while Ying Ji’s betrayal of Lü Lu earned the eternal label of friend-seller.

sentences.zh: 亦所以激揚風俗，弘長名教。

translations.literal: This also is what stirs and raises custom, enlarges and lengthens name-teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Both episodes stirred public mores and reinforced moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 王彬艤船而厚其所薄，王舒沈江而薄其所厚，較之優劣，斷乎可知。

translations.literal: Wang Bin moored boats and was generous to those he despised; Wang Shu drowned men in the river and was harsh to those he favored—comparing their superiority and inferiority, the break is surely knowable.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin quietly readied boats for kin he scorned; Wang Shu drowned kin he favored—whose conduct was nobler is plain.

sentences.zh: 思行、彪之厲風規於多僻之日，虞潭、顧衆徇貞心于危蹙之辰。

translations.literal: Sixing and Biao zhi enforced integrity in an age of many depravities; Yu Tan and Gu Zhong gave loyal hearts in hours of peril.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Mo and Wang Biao zhi held the line in a decadent age; Yu Tan and Gu Zhong risked everything when the throne tottered.

sentences.zh: 龍管為出納之端，{制魚}魚非獻替之術，嘯父之對，何其鄙歟！

translations.literal: The dragon tube is the beginning of receipts and payments; {制魚} fish is not the art of remonstrance and replacement—how base was Xiaofu’s answer!
translations.idiomatic: Treasury clerks handle accounts; salted fish is no substitute for frank counsel—how petty Yu Xiaofu’s seaside reply looks beside such men!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：處明夙令，聲頹暮年。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Chuming was wise from youth, his fame waned only in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Wang Shu shone early, though his star faded late in life.

sentences.zh: 允之騂角，無棄山川。

translations.literal: Yunzhi in colt’s years did not abandon rivers and mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yunzhi from boyhood never flinched from field and flood.

sentences.zh: 廙稱多藝，綢繆哲後。

translations.literal: Yi was praised for many arts, intimately bound with a wise later ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi’s brilliance bound him to a shrewd young sovereign.

sentences.zh: 二三其德，亦孔之醜。

translations.literal: Now this virtue, now that—how ugly is such inconstancy.
translations.idiomatic: His wavering loyalty matched the Book of Songs’ warning against “two-three virtues”—an ugly stain.

sentences.zh: 世儒憤發，慟顗陵敦。

translations.literal: Shiru blazed with rage, weeping for Yi before Dun’s fury.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin’s outburst, mourning Zhou Yi under Wang Dun’s glare, awed his age.

sentences.zh: 彪之不撓，甯浩旋溫。

translations.literal: Biao zhi did not bend; only then did Yin Hao turn and Huan Wen wheel about.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biao zhi’s iron spine checked Yin Hao and turned Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 顧實南金，虞惟東箭。

translations.literal: Gu was true southern gold; Yu alone the eastern arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zhong was southern gold; Yu Tan the eastern arrow of Wu.

sentences.zh: 銑質無改，筠心不變，公望公才，𩦎為其選。

translations.literal: Xian substance without change, Yun heart without change; for public repute and public talent, Mo was the choice.
translations.idiomatic: Refined mettle unbent, a heart straight as bamboo—when the age needed both prestige and ability, Yu Mo was the man they chose.”
